sentences.zh: 推入紀法：置上元庚辰盡所求年，以元法除之，不滿元法，以紀法除之，余不滿紀法，入紀年也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing entry into an era: set the gengchen upper origin and exhaust the year sought; divide by the origin divisor; what does not fill the origin divisor, divide by the era divisor; the remainder that does not fill the era divisor is the year of entry into the era.
translations.idiomatic: To find which era-year you are in: count from the gengchen upper origin to the target year, divide by 3,648; take the remainder and divide by 608; the final remainder is the year within the current era.

sentences.zh: 滿法去之，得後紀。

translations.literal: When it fills the divisor, remove it to obtain the next era.
translations.idiomatic: When the remainder equals the divisor, drop one full cycle and advance to the next era.

sentences.zh: 入甲午紀壬辰歲來，至今元嘉二十年歲在癸末，二百三十一年，算外。

translations.literal: From entry into the jiawu era in the renchen year to the present, the twentieth year of Yuanjia in the year guiwei, is 231 years, outside the count.
translations.idiomatic: From entering the jiawu era (renchen year) down to Yuanjia year 20 (guiwei) is 231 years—exclusive of the count.

sentences.zh: 推積月術：置入紀年數算外，以章月乘之，如章歲為積月，不盡為閏餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing accumulated months: set the year-of-entry number outside the count; multiply by rule months; divide by rule years for accumulated months; what does not exhaust is the intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find accumulated months: take the era-year count (exclusive), multiply by 235, divide by 19; the quotient is accumulated months, the remainder the intercalary surplus.

sentences.zh: 閏餘十二以上，其年閏。

translations.literal: If the intercalary remainder is twelve or more, that year has an intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: If the intercalary remainder is 12 or greater, declare a leap month that year.

sentences.zh: 推朔術：以通數乘積分，為朔積分，滿日法為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing new moons: multiply accumulated months by the communication number for the accumulated new-moon fraction; what fills the day divisor is accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To compute conjunction instants: multiply accumulated months by 22,207; divide by 752 for whole days; the residue is the fractional day.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積日，不盡為大餘，命以紀，算外，所求年正月朔日也。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the great remainder; name it from the era, outside the count—that is the new moon of the first month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Strip full 60-day cycles from the day-count; the residue is the stem-branch date; name it from the era cycle—this gives the first-month new moon of the target year.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加大餘二十九，小餘三百九十九，小余滿日法從大餘，即次月朔也。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add twenty-nine to the great remainder and 399 to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry into the great remainder—that is the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month, add 29 days and 399 parts; when the fractional parts exceed 752, carry one day—this yields the next new moon.

sentences.zh: 小餘三百五十三以上，其月大也。

translations.literal: If the small remainder is 353 or more, that month is long.
translations.idiomatic: If the fractional remainder is 353 or greater, the month is a long (30-day) month.

sentences.zh: 推弦望法：加朔大餘七，小餘二百八十七，小分三，小分滿四從小余，小余滿日法從大餘，命如前，上弦日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing quarter moons: add seven to the new-moon great remainder and 287 to the small remainder and three to the small parts; when small parts fill four, carry into the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry into the great remainder; name as before—that is the first-quarter day.
translations.idiomatic: To find the first quarter: add 7 days, 287 parts, and 3 small parts to the new-moon date; carry fractions as needed—that gives the first-quarter day.

sentences.zh: 又加之得望，又加之得下弦。

translations.literal: Add again to obtain full moon; add again to obtain last quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the same addition for full moon and again for last quarter.

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣術：置入紀年算外，以餘數乘之，滿度法三百四為積沒，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the twenty-four qi: set the year-of-entry outside the count; multiply by the remainder number; what fills the degree divisor 304 is accumulated extinction; what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find the twenty-four solar terms: take the era-year count (exclusive), multiply by 1,595; divide by 304 for whole cycles; the residue is the fractional part.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積沒，不盡為大餘，命以紀，算外，所求年雨水日也。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated extinction; what does not exhaust is the great remainder; name from the era, outside the count—that is the Rain Water day of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Remove 60-day cycles; the residue names the stem-branch date from the era—that is the Rain Water (yushui) of the target year.

sentences.zh: 求次氣，加大餘十五，小餘六十六，小分十一，小分滿氣法從小余，小余滿度法從大餘，次氣日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next qi, add fifteen to the great remainder, sixty-six to the small remainder, and eleven to the small parts; when small parts fill the qi divisor, carry into the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the degree divisor, carry into the great remainder—that is the next qi day.
translations.idiomatic: For the next term, add 15 days, 66 parts, and 11 small parts, carrying fractions through the qi and degree divisors.

sentences.zh: 雨水在十六日以後者，如法減之，得立春。

translations.literal: If Rain Water falls after the sixteenth day, reduce by the method to obtain Start of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: If Rain Water falls after the 16th, apply the correction formula to obtain Start of Spring (lichun).

sentences.zh: 推閏月法：以閏余減章歲，餘以歲中乘之，滿章閏得一，數從正月起，閏所在也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing intercalary months: subtract rule years from the intercalary remainder; multiply the remainder by mid-year qi; divide by rule intercalations for one; count from the first month—the intercalation lies there.
translations.idiomatic: To locate the leap month: subtract 19 from the intercalary surplus, multiply by 12, divide by 7; count forward from month 1.

sentences.zh: 閏有進退，以無中氣禦之。

translations.literal: Intercalations may advance or retreat; govern them by the absence of a mid-term qi.
translations.idiomatic: Leap-month placement may shift; a month without a mid-climate qi must be intercalary.

sentences.zh: 推沒滅術：因雨水積，以沒餘乘之，滿沒法為大餘，不盡為小餘，如前，所求年為雨水前沒日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing extinction and annihilation: take the Rain Water accumulation; multiply by the extinction remainder; what fills the extinction divisor is the great remainder; what does not exhaust is the small remainder; as before—that is the extinction day before Rain Water of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: To find extinction days: from the Rain Water accumulation, multiply by 36; divide by 319 for whole days; the residue names the pre-Rain Water extinction day.

sentences.zh: 求次沒，加大餘六十九，小餘一百九十六，滿沒法從大餘，命如前，雨水後沒日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next extinction, add sixty-nine to the great remainder and 196 to the small remainder; when it fills the extinction divisor, carry into the great remainder; name as before—that is the extinction day after Rain Water.
translations.idiomatic: For the next extinction, add 69 days and 196 parts, carrying when the divisor is exceeded.

sentences.zh: 雨水前沒多在故歲，常有五沒，官以沒正之，一年常有五沒或六沒。

translations.literal: Extinctions before Rain Water mostly fall in the previous year; there are regularly five extinctions; the office corrects by extinction—one year regularly has five or six extinctions.
translations.idiomatic: Pre-Rain Water extinctions usually belong to the prior year; normally there are five per year, sometimes six, as the calendar office adjusts.

sentences.zh: 小餘盡為滅日也。

translations.literal: When the small remainder is exhausted, it is an annihilation day.
translations.idiomatic: When the fractional remainder reaches zero, that day is an annihilation (mie) day.

sentences.zh: 雨水小餘三十九以還，雨水六旬後乃有。

translations.literal: When Rain Water's small remainder is 39 or less, the extinction comes only after six decades following Rain Water.
translations.idiomatic: If Rain Water's fractional part is 39 or below, the first extinction appears only after 60 days past Rain Water.

sentences.zh: 推土用事法：置立春大小餘小分之數，減大餘十八，小餘七十九，小分十八，命以紀，算外，立春前土用事日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing earth's dominance: set the great and small remainders and small parts of Start of Spring; subtract eighteen from the great remainder, seventy-nine from the small remainder, and eighteen from the small parts; name from the era, outside the count—that is the earth-dominance day before Start of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: To find when earth element dominates: from Start of Spring's date parts, subtract 18 days, 79 parts, and 18 small parts—this names the pre-lichun earth-dominance day.

sentences.zh: 大餘不足加六十，小餘不足減，減大餘一，加度法而後減之。

translations.literal: If the great remainder is insufficient, add sixty; if the small remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the great remainder, add the degree divisor, then subtract.
translations.idiomatic: Borrow 60 days when needed; borrow one degree-divisor (304 parts) when fractional subtraction underflows.

sentences.zh: 立夏、立冬求土用事皆如上法。

translations.literal: Start of Summer and Start of Winter earth-dominance are all found by the method above.
translations.idiomatic: Earth dominance at Start of Summer and Start of Winter uses the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 推日所在度法：以度法乘朔積度，不盡為分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the du where the sun stands: multiply the new-moon accumulated du by the degree divisor; what does not exhaust is parts.
translations.idiomatic: To find the sun's lodge position: multiply accumulated du by 304; the remainder is fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 命度起室二，次宿除之，算外，正月朔夜半日在度及分也。

translations.literal: Name the du starting from Room II; remove successive lodges; outside the count—that is the du and parts where the sun stood at midnight on the first-month new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Count lodges from Room 2; the remainder gives the midnight solar position on the first-month new moon.

sentences.zh: 求次日，日加一度，經室去度分。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one du per day; when passing through Room, remove the degree parts.
translations.idiomatic: Each day add one du; apply the Room-lodge correction to the fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 推月所在度法：以月周乘朔積日，周天去之，余滿度法為積度，不盡為分，命度如前，正月朔夜半月所在度及分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the du where the moon stands: multiply the new-moon accumulated days by the lunar circuit; remove the circumference days; the remainder that fills the degree divisor is accumulated du; what does not exhaust is parts; name the du as before—that is the du and parts where the moon stood at midnight on the first-month new moon.
translations.idiomatic: For the moon's lodge: multiply accumulated days by 4,064, reduce modulo 111,025, convert to du and parts—this gives midnight lunar position on the first-month new moon.

sentences.zh: 求次月，小月加度二十二，分一百三十三，大月加度三十五，分二百四十五，分滿度法成一度，命如前，次月朔月所在度及分也。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, for a short month add twenty-two du and 133 parts; for a long month add thirty-five du and 245 parts; when parts fill the degree divisor, form one du; name as before—that is the du and parts where the moon stands on the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month: add 22 du 133 parts (short month) or 35 du 245 parts (long month), carrying at 304 parts per du.

sentences.zh: 曆先月法：以十六除月行分為大分，如所入遲疾加之，經室去度分。

translations.literal: Calendar's advance-month method: divide the moon's motion parts by sixteen for great parts; add according to the slow-fast entered; when passing through Room, remove the degree parts.
translations.idiomatic: Advance-month correction: divide lunar motion parts by 16, then add the slow-fast increment for the day entered; apply Room-lodge reduction.

sentences.zh: 推合朔月食術：置所求年積月，以會數一百六十乘之，以所入交會紀差二十二加之，滿會月去之，餘則其年正月朔去交分也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing conjunction and lunar eclipse: set the accumulated months of the year sought; multiply by the coincidence number 160; add the crossing-coincidence discrepancy of the era entered, 22; when it fills coincidence months, remove it; the remainder is the distance from crossing at the first-month new moon of that year.
translations.idiomatic: For syzygy and eclipse limits: multiply year-months by 160, add the era's node offset (22), reduce modulo 929—the remainder is the new moon's distance from the lunar node.

sentences.zh: 求次月，以會數加之，滿會月去之。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add the coincidence number; when it fills coincidence months, remove it.
translations.idiomatic: Each month add 160, reducing modulo 929.

sentences.zh: 求望，加合數。

translations.literal: To seek full moon, add the coincidence number.
translations.idiomatic: For full moon, add the new-full coincidence number (80).

sentences.zh: 朔望去交分如合數以下，交限數以上，朔則交會，望則月食。

translations.literal: If the new or full moon's distance from crossing is at or below the coincidence number but at or above the crossing-limit number, new moon means conjunction and full moon means lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If the node distance is between 80 and 859, expect a solar eclipse at new moon or a lunar eclipse at full moon.

sentences.zh: 推入遲疾曆法：置所求年朔積分，所入遲疾差一萬五千二百四十五加之，滿通周去之，余滿日法得一日，不盡為日餘，命日算外，所求年正月朔入曆。

translations.literal: Method for pushing entry into the slow-fast calendar: set the new-moon accumulated fraction of the year sought; add the slow-fast discrepancy of the era entered, 15,245; when it fills the communication circuit, remove it; the remainder that fills the day divisor gives one day; what does not exhaust is the day remainder; name the day outside the count—that is entry into the calendar at the first-month new moon of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: To enter the slow-fast table: take the new-moon accumulated fraction, add the era's offset (15,245 for jiawu), reduce modulo 20,721, then divide by 752 for the calendar day and remainder at the year's first new moon.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加一日，日餘七百三十四。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add one day and 734 to the day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Each month advance one calendar day and 734 parts.

sentences.zh: 求望，加十四日，日餘五百七十五半。

translations.literal: To seek full moon, add fourteen days and 575½ to the day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For full moon, add 14 days and 575½ parts.

sentences.zh: 余滿日法成一日，日滿二十七去之，除日余如周日日餘，不足減，減一日，加周虛。

translations.literal: When the remainder fills the day divisor, form one day; when days fill twenty-seven, remove them; for the day remainder, act as with the circuit-day day remainder; if insufficient to subtract, subtract one day and add the circuit void.
translations.idiomatic: Carry when parts exceed 752; every 27 days drop a cycle; near circuit-day apply the 417/335 correction.

sentences.zh: 日滿二十七而日余不滿周日日餘，為損。

translations.literal: When days fill twenty-seven but the day remainder does not fill the circuit-day day remainder, it is a deficit.
translations.idiomatic: At the 27-day boundary, if the remainder falls short of 417, record a deficit (sun).

sentences.zh: 周日滿去之，為入曆一日。

translations.literal: When the circuit day is full, remove it to enter the calendar for one day.
translations.idiomatic: When the circuit-day correction completes, advance one day in the slow-fast calendar.

sentences.zh: 推合朔月食定大小餘法：以入曆日餘乘入曆下損益率，入一日，益二十五是也。

translations.literal: Method for fixing large and small remainders for conjunction and lunar eclipse: multiply the day remainder entered in the calendar by the increase-decrease rate under that calendar entry; entering day one, increase twenty-five is the rule.
translations.idiomatic: To fix syzygy and eclipse instants: multiply the anomalistic day fraction by the tabulated increase-decrease rate—for day 1 the rate is +25.

sentences.zh: 以損益盈縮積分，值損則損之，值益則益之。

translations.literal: With it increase or decrease the expansion-contraction accumulated parts; where decrease applies, decrease; where increase applies, increase.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the product to the expansion-contraction accumulated column, adding or subtracting according to whether the rate is surplus or deficit.

sentences.zh: 為定積分。

translations.literal: This becomes the fixed accumulated parts.
translations.idiomatic: The result is the corrected integral.

sentences.zh: 以入曆日餘乘列差，滿日法盈減縮加差法，為定差法。

translations.literal: Multiply the day remainder entered in the calendar by the column difference; when it fills the day divisor, subtract expansion or add contraction to the difference divisor—this becomes the fixed difference divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the anomalistic fraction by the column difference; at each full day divisor, adjust the difference divisor by expansion or contraction to obtain the fixed divisor.

sentences.zh: 以除定積分，所得減加本朔望小餘，值盈則減，縮則加之。

translations.literal: Divide it into the fixed accumulated parts; what is obtained subtracts from or adds to the original new- or full-moon small remainder; where expansion applies, subtract; where contraction applies, add.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the corrected integral by the fixed difference divisor and apply the quotient to the base fractional day—subtract for expansion, add for contraction.

sentences.zh: 為定小餘。

translations.literal: This becomes the fixed small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: This yields the corrected fractional day.

sentences.zh: 加之滿日法，合朔月食進一日；

translations.literal: If adding fills the day divisor, the conjunction or lunar eclipse advances one day;
translations.idiomatic: A carry past the day divisor moves the syzygy or eclipse one day forward;

sentences.zh: 減之不足減者，加日法而後減之，則退一日。

translations.literal: If subtracting is insufficient, add the day divisor and then subtract—then retreat one day.
translations.idiomatic: If subtraction underflows, borrow one day divisor and step the date back one day.

sentences.zh: 值周日者，用周日定數。

translations.literal: When it falls on a circuit day, use the circuit-day fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: On a circuit-day entry, apply the circuit-day fixed constants instead.

sentences.zh: 推加時：以十二乘定小余，滿日法得一辰，數從子起，算外，則朔望加時所在辰也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the double-hour: multiply the fixed small remainder by twelve; what fills the day divisor obtains one chen; count from zi outward, outside the reckoning—this is the chen where the new- or full-moon hour falls.
translations.idiomatic: To name the hour of syzygy: multiply the corrected fraction by 12, divide by 752 for whole double-hours counted from midnight (zi).

sentences.zh: 有餘者四之，滿日法得一為少，二為半，三為太半。

translations.literal: If there is remainder, quadruple it; what fills the day divisor gives one shao, two gives ban, three gives tai-ban.
translations.idiomatic: Split any leftover into quarters of the day divisor for the shao, half, and tai-half subdivisions.

sentences.zh: 又有餘者三之，滿日法得一為強，半法以上排成一，不滿半法棄之。

translations.literal: If again there is remainder, triple it; what fills the day divisor gives one qiang; at half the divisor or above, advance one notch; below half the divisor, discard.
translations.idiomatic: Triple the tail again for the strong step, rounding up at half-divisor and discarding below.

sentences.zh: 以強並少為少強，並半為半強，並太為太強。

translations.literal: Combine qiang with shao to make shao-qiang; combine with ban to make ban-qiang; combine with tai to make tai-qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Add strong units to weak, half, and full subdivisions per the classical clepsydra notation.

sentences.zh: 得二者為小弱，以並少為半弱，以並半為太弱，以並太為一辰弱。

translations.literal: Obtaining two qiang makes xiao-ruo; combine with shao to make ban-ruo; combine with ban to make tai-ruo; combine with tai to make one chen-ruo.
translations.idiomatic: Two strongs collapse into a weak grade, stepping through the ladder to a full weak double-hour mark.

sentences.zh: 以所在辰名之。

translations.literal: Name it by the chen where it stands.
translations.idiomatic: Read the final label against the named double-hour.

sentences.zh: 推合朔月食加時滿刻法：各以百刻乘定小餘，如日法而一；

translations.literal: Method for pushing full clepsydra marks for the conjunction or lunar-eclipse hour: for each, multiply the fixed small remainder by one hundred clepsydra marks; divide by the day divisor;
translations.idiomatic: To convert syzygy time to clepsydra marks: multiply the corrected fractional day by 100 and divide by 752;

sentences.zh: 不盡什之，求分。

translations.literal: What is not exhausted, multiply by ten to obtain fen.
translations.idiomatic: Scale the remainder by ten to recover fractional marks.

sentences.zh: 先除夜漏之半，即晝漏加時刻及分也。

translations.literal: First remove half the night clepsydra—then the day clepsydra hour marks and fen appear.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract half the night-water total first; the remainder gives the daytime hour and fractional marks.

sentences.zh: 晝漏盡，又入夜漏。

translations.literal: When the day clepsydra is exhausted, enter the night clepsydra again.
translations.idiomatic: After the day-water runs out, continue into the night-water register.

sentences.zh: 在中節前後四日以還者，視限數。

translations.literal: Within four days before or after a mid-term node, consult the limit number.
translations.idiomatic: If the date lies within four days of a mid-climate, use the limit number.

sentences.zh: 在中節前後五日以上者，視間限數。

translations.literal: Five days or more before or after a mid-term node, consult the interval-limit number.
translations.idiomatic: If five or more days from a mid-climate, use the interval-limit number instead.

sentences.zh: 月食加時定小餘不滿限數、間數者，皆以算上為日。

translations.literal: When the lunar-eclipse hour fixed small remainder does not fill the limit or interval number, treat the computed day as the event day.
translations.idiomatic: If the eclipse-time fraction falls below the limit or interval threshold, count the syzygy on the computed calendar day.

sentences.zh: 小分一百三損二百二十四九萬三千四百八意差法二千

translations.literal: Small parts one hundred three; decrease two hundred twenty-four; ninety-three thousand four hundred eight; increase; difference divisor two thousand
translations.idiomatic: Table continuation: small parts 103; deficit rate 224; accumulated surplus 93,408; excess; difference divisor 2,000

sentences.zh: 三百九

translations.literal: three hundred nine
translations.idiomatic: 309 (completing difference divisor 2,309).

sentences.zh: 推合朔度：以章歲乘朔小余，滿通法為大分，不盡為小分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing conjunction longitude: multiply the new-moon small remainder by rule years; what fills the communication divisor becomes large fractional parts; what does not exhaust is small fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: To find syzygy longitude: multiply the conjunction fractional day by 19; divide by 47 for large fractional parts and keep the remainder as small fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 以大分從朔夜半日日分，滿度命如前，正月朔日月合朔所在共合度也。

translations.literal: Add the large fractional parts to the new-moon midnight daily degree parts; when parts fill the degree divisor, carry into du; count the du as before—the longitude where sun and moon conjoin at the first-month new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Add the large parts to the midnight solar position on new-moon day, carrying at 304 parts per du—the result is the first-month conjunction longitude.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加度二十九，大分一百六十一，小分十四，小分滿通法從大分，大分滿度法從度。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add twenty-nine du, large parts one hundred sixty-one, and small parts fourteen; when small parts fill the communication divisor, carry into large parts; when large parts fill the degree divisor, carry into du.
translations.idiomatic: Each month add 29 du, 161 large parts, and 14 small parts, carrying through the communication and degree divisors.

sentences.zh: 經室除度分。

translations.literal: Passing through Room, remove the lodge fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: When crossing the Room lodge, subtract its fractional correction.

sentences.zh: 求望，加十四度，大分二百三十二，小分三十半。

translations.literal: To seek full moon, add fourteen du, large parts two hundred thirty-two, and small parts thirty and a half.
translations.idiomatic: For full moon, add 14 du, 232 large parts, and 30½ small parts.

sentences.zh: 求望月所在度，加日度一百八十二，分一百八十九，小分二十三半。

translations.literal: To seek the du where the full moon stands, add to the daily du one hundred eighty-two du, parts one hundred eighty-nine, and small parts twenty-three and a half.
translations.idiomatic: For the full-moon position, add 182 du, 189 parts, and 23½ small parts to the solar longitude.

translations.literal: Conjunction years, conjunction count, daily-degree divisor, lodge fractional parts: Wood—344, 315, 95,762, 23,625; Fire—459, 215, 65,361, 16,125; Earth—383, 371, 112,482, 77,750; Metal—267, 167, 50,768, 12,525; Water—79, 249, 75,696, 18,675.
translations.idiomatic: Planetary cycle constants (conjunction years / conjunction count / daily-degree divisor / lodge fractional parts): Wood 344 / 315 / 95,762 / 23,625; Fire 459 / 215 / 65,361 / 16,125; Earth 383 / 371 / 112,482 / 77,750; Metal 267 / 167 / 50,768 / 12,525; Water 79 / 249 / 75,696 / 18,675.

sentences.zh: 火後元乙亥，元嘉十二年，至元嘉二十年癸未，九年算上。

translations.literal: Fire later origin: yihai; Yuanjia year 12 to Yuanjia year 20 guiwei—nine years, outside the count.
translations.idiomatic: Fire's later origin (yihai): from Yuanjia 12 to Yuanjia 20 (guiwei) is 9 years—exclusive of the count.

sentences.zh: 土後元甲戌，元嘉十一年，至元嘉二十年癸未，十年算上。

translations.literal: Earth later origin: jiaxu; Yuanjia year 11 to Yuanjia year 20 guiwei—ten years, outside the count.
translations.idiomatic: Earth's later origin (jiaxu): from Yuanjia 11 to Yuanjia 20 (guiwei) is 10 years—exclusive of the count.

sentences.zh: 金後元甲申，晉太元九年，至元嘉二十年癸未，六十年算上。

translations.literal: Metal later origin: jiashen; Jin Taiyuan year 9 to Yuanjia year 20 guiwei—sixty years, outside the count.
translations.idiomatic: Metal's later origin (jiashen): from Jin Taiyuan 9 to Yuanjia 20 (guiwei) is 60 years—exclusive of the count.

sentences.zh: 水後元乙丑，元嘉二年，至元嘉二十年癸未，十九年算上。

translations.literal: Water later origin: yichou; Yuanjia year 2 to Yuanjia year 20 guiwei—nineteen years, outside the count.
translations.idiomatic: Water's later origin (yichou): from Yuanjia 2 to Yuanjia 20 (guiwei) is 19 years—exclusive of the count.

sentences.zh: 推五星法：各設其元至所求年算上，以合數乘之，滿合歲為積合，不盡曰合餘，多者以合數除之，得一，星合往年，得二，合前往年，不滿合數，其年。

translations.literal: Method for computing the five planets: for each, set its era origin to the year sought, outside the count; multiply by the conjunction count; what fills conjunction years is accumulated conjunction; what does not exhaust is called conjunction remainder; if it fills the conjunction count more than once, divide by the conjunction count—obtaining one means the star conjoined the prior year, two means the year before that; if it does not fill the conjunction count, conjunction falls in the current year.
translations.idiomatic: For each planet, count from its era origin to the target year, multiply by the conjunction count, and divide by conjunction years; the quotient is accumulated conjunctions, the remainder the conjunction surplus—one full cycle back means last year's conjunction, two means the year before, otherwise the current year.

sentences.zh: 木、土、金則有往年合，火有前往年合，水一年三合或四合也。

translations.literal: Wood, Earth, and Metal may conjoin in the prior year; Fire may conjoin in the year before that; Water may have three or four conjunctions in one year.
translations.idiomatic: Wood, Earth, and Metal can conjoin in the previous year; Fire may conjoin two years back; Water can have three or four conjunctions in a single year.

sentences.zh: 以合餘減合數為度分，水度分滿合歲則去之也。

translations.literal: Subtract the conjunction remainder from the conjunction count for degree parts; for Water, when degree parts fill conjunction years, remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Degree parts equal the conjunction count minus the conjunction remainder; for Water, reduce modulo conjunction years.

sentences.zh: 以周天十一萬一千三十五乘度分，滿日度法為積度，不盡曰度餘。

translations.literal: Multiply degree parts by the circuit heaven 111,035; what fills the daily-degree divisor becomes accumulated du; what does not exhaust is called degree remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the degree parts by 111,035, divide by the daily-degree divisor for whole du, and keep the residue as degree remainder.

sentences.zh: 命度以室二，算外，星合所在度也。

translations.literal: Count du from Room 2 outward, outside the reckoning—this is the du where the star conjoins.
translations.idiomatic: Name the conjunction longitude from Room 2—exclusive of the count.

sentences.zh: 以合數乘其年，內雨水小餘，並度余為日余，滿日度法從積度為日，命以雨水，算外，星合日也。

translations.literal: Multiply the conjunction count by the year count; include the Rain Water small remainder; add the degree remainder for the day remainder; when it fills the daily-degree divisor, carry into accumulated du for the day; count from Rain Water outward, outside the reckoning—this is the star-conjunction day.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply years by the conjunction count, add Rain Water's fractional day and the degree remainder, carry into whole days, and name the date from Rain Water.

sentences.zh: 求星見日法，以法伏日及餘木則十六日及金是也。

translations.literal: Method for finding the star-appearance day: use the occultation days and remainder from the method—for Wood it is sixteen days and remainder, and for Metal likewise.
translations.idiomatic: To find first visibility: take the tabulated occultation days and remainder—Wood uses 16 days (Metal likewise).

sentences.zh: 加星合日及余，滿日度法成一日，命如前，星見日也。

translations.literal: Add to the star-conjunction day and remainder; when it fills the daily-degree divisor, form one day; count as before—this is the star-appearance day.
translations.idiomatic: Add the occultation interval to the conjunction date, carrying at the daily-degree divisor, to obtain the appearance day.

sentences.zh: 求星見度法，以法伏度及餘木則二度及餘是也。

translations.literal: Method for finding the star-appearance du: use the occultation du and remainder from the method—for Wood it is two du and remainder, likewise.
translations.idiomatic: For appearance longitude: add the tabulated occultation arc—for Wood, 2 du plus remainder.

sentences.zh: 加星合度及余，滿日度法成一度，命如前，所見度也。

translations.literal: Add to the star-conjunction du and remainder; when it fills the daily-degree divisor, form one du; count as before—this is the du where it appears.
translations.idiomatic: Add the occultation arc to the conjunction longitude, carrying at the daily-degree divisor, to obtain the appearance position.

sentences.zh: 以星行分母木則二十三見也。

translations.literal: Use the star-motion divisor—for Wood it is twenty-three at appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Take the star-motion denominator—Wood uses 23 from first appearance onward.

sentences.zh: 乘見度余，滿日度法得一，分乃日加所行分。

translations.literal: Multiply the appearance-degree remainder; when it fills the daily-degree divisor, obtain one fen; then daily add the motion fen.
translations.idiomatic: Scale the appearance remainder by the motion rate: each time it fills the daily-degree divisor, advance one fen of daily motion.

sentences.zh: 木順日行四分。

translations.literal: Wood: in direct motion, daily motion four fen.
translations.idiomatic: Wood: direct motion at 4 fen per day.

sentences.zh: 分滿其母成一度，逆順母不同，木逆分母七也。

translations.literal: When fen fill the divisor, form one du; direct and retrograde divisors differ—for Wood the retrograde divisor is seven.
translations.idiomatic: Carry at the motion divisor to whole du; direct and retrograde phases use different divisors—Wood retrograde uses 7.

sentences.zh: 當各乘度餘，留者承前，逆則減之，伏不書度，經室去分，不足減者，破全度。

translations.literal: Each should multiply the degree remainder; during stationary phases continue the prior value; in retrograde subtract; during occultation do not record du; passing Room remove fen; if insufficient to subtract, break a whole du.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the motion increment to the degree remainder; hold position through stations, subtract in retrograde, omit degrees while hidden, subtract Room lodge parts, and borrow a whole du when needed.

sentences.zh: 五星室分各異，若在行分，各依室分去之。

translations.literal: The five planets' lodge fractional parts each differ; if in motion parts, each removes them according to its lodge fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: Each planet has its own lodge fractional correction—apply the appropriate reduction whenever motion parts cross a lodge boundary.

sentences.zh: 木：初與日合，伏，十六日，日余四萬一千七百八十，行二度，余七萬七千八百四十七半，晨見東方。

translations.literal: Wood: at first conjunction with the sun, occultation sixteen days, day remainder 41,780, motion two du, degree remainder 77,847½; morning appearance in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Wood: after initial conjunction it is hidden 16 days (day remainder 41,780), moves 2 du (remainder 77,847½), then appears in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 去日十三度半強。

translations.literal: Distance from the sun thirteen du and a half qiang.
translations.idiomatic: It stands 13½ du strong from the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，日行二十三分之四，一百一十五日行二十度。

translations.literal: Direct motion: daily motion four parts of twenty-three; in one hundred fifteen days it moves twenty du.
translations.idiomatic: Direct: 4/23 du per day, 20 du in 115 days.

sentences.zh: 留，不行，二十六日而逆。

translations.literal: Stationary—no motion—for twenty-six days, then retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: It stations 26 days, then turns retrograde.

sentences.zh: 日行七分之一，八十四日退十二度。

translations.literal: Daily motion one part of seven; in eighty-four days it retreats twelve du.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde: 1/7 du per day, 12 du in 84 days.

sentences.zh: 又留二十六日。

translations.literal: Again stationary twenty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: It stations another 26 days.

sentences.zh: 順，一百一十五日行二十度，夕伏西方，日度余如初，與日合。

translations.literal: Direct motion: in one hundred fifteen days it moves twenty du; evening hiding in the west; solar degree remainder as at first; conjunction with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Direct again for 115 days and 20 du, then hides at dusk in the west and rejoins the sun with the original remainder.

sentences.zh: 一終三百九十八日，日余八萬三千五百六十，行星三十三度，余五萬九千九百三十五。

translations.literal: One cycle: three hundred ninety-eight days, day remainder 83,560; planetary motion thirty-three du, degree remainder 59,935.
translations.idiomatic: One synodic cycle: 398 days (remainder 83,560), heliocentric motion 33 du (remainder 59,935).

sentences.zh: 火：初與日合，伏，七十一日，日余二萬四千八百一十二半，行五十四度，度余四萬九千四百三十，晨見東方。

translations.literal: Fire: at first conjunction with the sun, occultation seventy-one days, day remainder 24,812½, motion fifty-four du, degree remainder 49,430; morning appearance in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Fire: hidden 71 days (remainder 24,812½), moves 54 du (remainder 49,430), then appears at dawn in the east.

sentences.zh: 去日十七度半強。

translations.literal: Distance from the sun seventeen du and a half qiang.
translations.idiomatic: It stands 17½ du strong from the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，疾，日行七分之五，一百八日半行七十七度半。

sentences.zh: 一終一百一十五日，日余六萬六千七百二十五，行星如之。

translations.idiomatic: One synodic cycle: 115 days (remainder 66,725), heliocentric motion matching.

sentences.zh: 一合五十七日，日余七萬一千二百一十半，行星亦如之。

translations.literal: One conjunction: fifty-seven days, day remainder 71,210½; planetary motion likewise.
translations.idiomatic: One inferior conjunction: 57 days (remainder 71,210½) with matching arc motion.

sentences.zh: 盈加縮減，十六除月行分，日法除盈縮分，以減度分，盈加縮減。

translations.literal: Surplus add, deficit subtract; divide lunar motion parts by sixteen; divide surplus-deficit parts by the day divisor; subtract from degree parts; surplus add, deficit subtract.
translations.idiomatic: Apply surplus to add and deficit to subtract; scale lunar motion by 16 and surplus-deficit by the day divisor, then adjust the degree fraction accordingly.

sentences.zh: 推卦：因雨水大小余，加大餘六，小餘三百一十九，小余滿三千六百四十八成日。

translations.literal: Method for pushing hexagrams: from Rain Water large and small remainders, add six to the large remainder and 319 to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills 3,648, form one day.
translations.idiomatic: To assign hexagram rulership: take Rain Water's sexagenary line and fractional day, add 6 days and 319 parts, and carry at 3,648 parts per day.

sentences.zh: 日滿二十七日餘不足加減不加周虛。

translations.literal: When days fill twenty-seven, if the remainder is insufficient for addition or subtraction, do not add the circuit void.
translations.idiomatic: At the 27-day limit, if the remainder cannot absorb the adjustment, omit the circuit-void correction.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年，承天奏上尚書：「今既改用《元嘉曆》，漏刻與先不同，宜應改革。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Yuanjia, Cheng Tian memorialized to the Secretariat of the Master of Writing: "Now that the Yuanjia Calendar has been adopted, the clepsydra gradations differ from before and ought to be reformed."
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 20, He Chengtian submitted to the Secretariat: "The Yuanjia Calendar is now in force, and its clepsydra periods no longer match the old ones—they should be revised."

sentences.zh: 按《景初曆》春分日長，秋分日短，相承所用漏刻，冬至後晝漏率長於冬至前。

translations.literal: According to the Jingchu Calendar, the spring-equinox day is long and the autumn-equinox day short; the clepsydra gradations handed down in succession make the daytime clepsydra after the winter solstice on average longer than before the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingchu Calendar holds that spring days are long and autumn days short, yet the inherited clepsydra tables make post-solstice daytime water run longer on average than pre-solstice—

sentences.zh: 且長短增減，進退無漸，非唯先法不精，亦各傳寫謬誤。

translations.literal: Moreover the lengthening and shortening increase and decrease with no gradual transition—not only is the former method imprecise, but each copy also contains transcription errors.
translations.idiomatic: and the shifts come in abrupt jumps rather than smooth steps. The old method was imprecise to begin with, and every hand-copied table added its own mistakes.

sentences.zh: 今二至二分，各據其正。

translations.literal: Now the two solstices and two equinoxes each rest on their proper values.
translations.idiomatic: We have now anchored the two solstices and two equinoxes each to its true position.

sentences.zh: 則至之前後，無複差異。

translations.literal: Then before and after each solstice there is no further discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after each solstice, the gradations no longer disagree.

sentences.zh: 更增損舊刻，參以晷影，刪定為經，改用二十五箭。

translations.literal: Further increase and decrease the old gradations, consult the gnomon shadow, edit and fix them as the standard, and adopt twenty-five arrow-tubes instead.
translations.idiomatic: We adjusted the old marks against sundial shadows, fixed them as the canonical scale, and replaced the tubes with a twenty-five-arrow clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 請台勒漏郎將考驗施用。

translations.literal: We request that the Directorate commission the Clepsydra Officer to examine and put it into use.
translations.idiomatic: We ask the Directorate to have the Clepsydra Officer test the new scale and put it into service.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 前世諸儒依圖緯雲，月行有九道。

translations.literal: Scholars of former ages, relying on the charts and apocrypha, held that the moon travels nine paths.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars, guided by cosmological charts and apocrypha, taught that the moon follows nine paths.

sentences.zh: 故畫作九規，更相交錯，檢其行次，遲疾換易，不得順度。

translations.literal: Therefore they drew nine circles intersecting one another; checking the sequence of motion, fast and slow alternated and changed, and the motion could not follow a single regular degree.
translations.idiomatic: They drew nine interlocking circles—but when one traced the moon's actual sequence, speed and slowness swapped places and the motion refused to obey a single uniform arc.

sentences.zh: 劉向論九道雲：「青道二出黃道東，白道二出黃道西，黑道二出北，赤道二出南。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's discussion of the nine paths states: "The green path emerges twice east of the yellow path; the white path emerges twice west of the yellow path; the black path emerges twice to the north; the red path emerges twice to the south."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang wrote on the nine paths: "Two green paths rise east of the ecliptic, two white paths west, two black paths north, and two red paths south."

sentences.zh: 」又雲：「立春、春分，東從青道；

translations.literal: " He also said: "At Start of Spring and the spring equinox, the moon follows the green path from the east;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "From Start of Spring through the spring equinox, the moon rides the green path from the east;

sentences.zh: 立夏、夏至，南從赤道。

translations.literal: at Start of Summer and the summer solstice, it follows the red path from the south.
translations.idiomatic: from Start of Summer through the summer solstice, it rides the red path from the south.

sentences.zh: 秋白冬黑，各隨其方。

translations.literal: In autumn it is white; in winter black—each according to its quarter.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn the white path, in winter the black—each in its season.

sentences.zh: 」按日行黃道，陽路也，月者陰精，不由陽路，故或出其外，或入其內，出入去黃道不得過六度。

translations.literal: " The sun travels the yellow path, the road of yang; the moon is the essence of yin and does not follow the road of yang. Therefore it sometimes emerges outside or enters inside; its departure from the yellow path may not exceed six du.
translations.idiomatic: The sun keeps to the ecliptic—the highway of yang—while the moon, being yin, does not. It swings outside or dips inside, but never more than six du from the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 入十三日有奇而出，出亦十三日有奇而入，凡二十七日而一入一出矣。

translations.literal: After thirteen days and a fraction it emerges; after emerging, thirteen days and a fraction again to re-enter—in all twenty-seven days for one entry and one exit.
translations.idiomatic: It takes a little over thirteen days to enter, and the same to exit again—twenty-seven days for a full in-and-out cycle.

sentences.zh: 交于黃道之上，與日相掩，則蝕焉。

translations.literal: Where it crosses the yellow path and meets the sun, an eclipse occurs.
translations.idiomatic: When it crosses the ecliptic and meets the sun, an eclipse follows.

sentences.zh: 漢世劉洪推檢月行，作陰陽曆法。

translations.literal: In the Han era Liu Hong examined and checked lunar motion and composed the yin-yang calendar method.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年，太祖使著作令史吳癸依洪法，制新術，令太史施用之。

translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 20, Emperor Wen ordered Compiler Clerk Wu Gui to adapt Liu Hong's method into a new procedure and put it in the hands of the Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 大分滿周天去之，余不滿曆周者為入陽曆。

translations.literal: When large fraction fills circuit heaven remove it; if the remainder does not fill the calendar circuit, it is entry into the yang calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce modulo circuit heaven; a remainder under the calendar circuit places the moon in the yang (north) column.

sentences.zh: 余皆如月周得一日，算外，所求年正月合朔入曆也。

translations.literal: The remainder all like the lunar circuit obtains one day, outside the count—the first-month conjunction entry into the calendar of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the residue by the lunar circuit for whole days beyond the tally—that is the first-month syzygy index in the table.

sentences.zh: 不盡為日餘。

translations.literal: What is not exhausted is the day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: What remains is the fractional day inside the table.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加二日，日餘一千三百三十一，微分一千五百九十八，如法成日，日滿十三去之，除日餘如分日。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add two days, day remainder 1,331, micro-fraction 1,598; by the method form days; when days fill thirteen remove them; remove the day remainder according to the split day.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 2 days, remainder 1,331, and micro-part 1,598, normalize, drop multiples of 13, and reconcile with the split-day rule.

sentences.zh: 陰陽曆竟平入端，入曆在前限餘前，後限餘後者，月行中道。

translations.literal: When the yin-yang calendar ends and levels into the terminal, if entry into the calendar falls before the front limit remainder or after the rear limit remainder, the moon moves on the middle path.
translations.idiomatic: When the solar-lunar cycle flips, if the index falls before the front limit or after the rear limit, the moon is taken to ride the ecliptic mean.

sentences.zh: 求朔弦望定數：各置入遲疾曆盈縮定積分，以章歲乘之，差法除之，所得滿通法為大分。

translations.literal: To seek the fixed numbers for new moon, first quarter, full moon, and last quarter: for each, set the slow-fast calendar surplus-deficit fixed accumulated parts; multiply by rule years; divide by the difference divisor; what is obtained filling the communication divisor becomes large fraction.
translations.idiomatic: To correct syzygy instants: take the slow-fast surplus-deficit integral, multiply by rule years (235), divide by the difference divisor, and carry whole parts at the communication divisor.

sentences.zh: 不盡，以微分法乘之，如法為微分。

translations.literal: What is not exhausted, multiply by the micro-fraction divisor; by the method obtain micro-fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Scale the remainder by the micro-fraction divisor to recover fine parts.

sentences.zh: 盈減縮加陰陽日餘，盈不足，以月周進退日而定，以定日餘乘損益兼數，為加時定數。

translations.literal: Surplus subtract, deficit add to the yin-yang day remainder; if surplus or deficit is insufficient, advance or retreat the day to fix it; multiply the fixed day remainder by the surplus-deficit combined number for the fixed number at the hour of addition.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract surplus and add deficit to the yin-yang day fraction, rolling the day forward or back if needed; multiply the corrected fraction by the paired adjustment for the true syzygy instant.

sentences.zh: 推夜半入曆：以差率朔小餘，如微分法得一，以減入曆餘，不足，加月周而減之，卻一日，卻得分日，加其分，半微分為小分，即朔日夜半入歷歷餘小分也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing midnight entry into the calendar: multiply the new-moon small remainder by the difference rate; as the micro-fraction divisor obtains one; subtract from the calendar-entry day remainder; if insufficient, add the lunar circuit and subtract; retreat one day; retreat and obtain the split day and add its fraction; half the micro-fraction becomes small fraction—the new-moon midnight calendar-entry remainder and small fraction.
translations.idiomatic: For midnight on new-moon day: scale the lunation fraction by the difference rate, divide by 1,878, subtract from the table remainder, borrowing the lunar circuit if needed; restore the split-day fraction and halve the fine part for the midnight index.

sentences.zh: 求次日，加一日，日餘十六，小分三百二十，小分如會從余，余滿月周去之，又加一日。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one day, day remainder sixteen, small fraction 320; small fraction like the conjunction number follows the remainder; when the remainder fills the lunar circuit remove it and again add one day.
translations.idiomatic: For the next day add 1 day, remainder 16, and small fraction 320 with carries through the conjunction number and lunar circuit.

sentences.zh: 曆竟，下日余滿分日去之，于入曆初也。

translations.literal: When the calendar ends, if the day remainder fills the split day remove it—this is at the calendar opening.
translations.idiomatic: At cycle bottom, clear split-day overflow to re-enter the table head.

sentences.zh: 不滿分日者，值之，加餘一千二百九十四，小分七百八十九半，為入次曆。

translations.literal: If it does not fill the split day, set it straight; add remainder 1,294, small fraction 789½, for entry into the next calendar.
translations.idiomatic: If the split-day slot is short, add 1,294 plus fractional 789½ to step into the next lunation row.

sentences.zh: 求夜半定日：以朔小余減入遲疾曆日餘，不足一日，卻得周日，加餘四百一十七，即月夜半入曆日及餘也。

translations.literal: To seek the fixed day at midnight: subtract the new-moon small remainder from the slow-fast calendar day remainder at midnight; if less than one day, retreat and obtain the circuit day, add remainder 417—the day and remainder of midnight entry into the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: For the true midnight date: subtract the syzygy fraction from the slow-fast midnight remainder; if under one day, borrow a circuit day and add 417 for the midnight table index.

sentences.zh: 以日餘乘損益率，盈縮積分，為定積分。

translations.literal: Multiply the day remainder by the surplus-deficit rate and the surplus-deficit accumulated parts for the fixed accumulated parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the day remainder by the rate and the surplus-deficit integral to obtain the corrected integral.

sentences.zh: 滿通法為大分，不盡以會月乘之，如法為小分，以盈加縮減入陰陽日餘，盈不足進退日而定也。

translations.literal: What fills the communication divisor becomes large fraction; what is not exhausted, multiply by conjunction months; by the method obtain small fraction; surplus add, deficit subtract from the yin-yang day remainder; if surplus or deficit is insufficient, advance or retreat the day to fix it.
translations.idiomatic: Carry at the communication divisor, scale the tail by conjunction months for small parts, adjust the yin-yang day count, and borrow a lunar-circuit day if needed.

sentences.zh: 以定日餘乘損益率，如月周，以損益兼數，為夜半定數。

translations.literal: Multiply the fixed day remainder by the surplus-deficit rate; as the lunar circuit obtains one; by surplus-deficit combined number—for the fixed number at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Scale the midnight remainder by the rate, divide by the lunar circuit, and apply the paired number for the true midnight correction.

sentences.zh: 求昏明數：以損益率乘所近節氣夜漏，二百而一為明，以減損益率為昏，而以損益夜半數為昏明定數也。

translations.literal: To seek the dusk and dawn numbers: multiply the surplus-deficit rate by the night clepsydra of the nearest solar term; two hundred and one for dawn; subtract from the surplus-deficit rate for dusk; and by surplus-deficit adjust the midnight number for the fixed dusk and dawn numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the rate by the night run of the neighboring qi and divide by 200 for dawn; subtract from the rate for dusk; combine with the midnight adjustment for definitive twilight values.

sentences.zh: 求月去黃道度：置加時若昏明定數，以十二除之為度，其餘三而一為少，不盡為強，二少弱也。

translations.literal: To seek the moon's distance from the yellow path in du: set the fixed number at the hour of addition or at dusk or dawn; divide by twelve for du; the remainder, three and one for shao; what is not exhausted, one for qiang; two shao is weak.
translations.idiomatic: Convert the correction to degrees by dividing by twelve, express thirds as shao and mark strong or weak units.

sentences.zh: 所得為月去黃道度。

translations.literal: What is obtained is the moon's distance from the yellow path in du.
translations.idiomatic: The result is the moon's ecliptic latitude.

sentences.zh: 大明六年，南徐州從事史祖沖之上表曰：

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daming, Attendant Clerk Zu Chongzhi of Southern Xuzhou submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 6, Zu Chongzhi, Attendant Clerk of Southern Xuzhou, submitted this memorial:

sentences.zh: 古曆疏舛，頗不精密，群氏糾紛，莫審其要。

translations.literal: The ancient calendars are coarse and erroneous, quite lacking in precision; the various schools dispute one another, and none can discern the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: The old calendars are rough and wrong—disputed by every school, yet none can say where the truth lies.

sentences.zh: 何承天所奏，意存改革，而置法簡略，今已乖遠。

translations.literal: What He Chengtian submitted aimed at reform, but the methods he established were oversimplified and are now far off the mark.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian meant to reform the system, but his methods were too spare—and time has already proved them inadequate.

sentences.zh: 以臣校之，三睹厥謬：日月所在，差覺三度；

translations.literal: By my reckoning I have thrice witnessed their errors: the positions of sun and moon differ by fully three du;
translations.idiomatic: I have checked them three times over and found the same failures: sun and moon positions miss by three full du;

sentences.zh: 二至晷影，幾失一日；

translations.literal: the gnomon shadows at the two solstices miss by nearly a whole day;
translations.idiomatic: solstice shadows are wrong by nearly a day;

sentences.zh: 五星見伏，至差四旬，留逆進退，或移兩宿。

translations.literal: the five planets' appearances and occultations miss by as much as forty days; their stations, retrogradations, advances, and retreats may shift by two lodges.
translations.idiomatic: planetary risings and settings drift by up to forty days, and stations and retrogrades wander two lodges off course.

sentences.zh: 分至乖失，則節閏非正；

translations.literal: When the quarter days and intercalations are wrong, the nodes and leap months are not correct;
translations.idiomatic: When solstice and equinox dates slip, intercalary months fall in the wrong place;

sentences.zh: 宿度違天，則伺察無准。

translations.literal: when the lodge degrees depart from Heaven, observation and verification have no standard.
translations.idiomatic: when lodge longitudes drift from the sky, observation loses all anchor.

sentences.zh: 臣生屬聖辰，逮在昌運，敢率愚瞽，更創新曆。

translations.literal: I was born in a sage reign and have reached an age of flourishing fortune; I dare, though blind and foolish, to create a new calendar anew.
translations.idiomatic: I was born under a sage throne, in an age of bright fortune—and though I am no more than a fool, I dare propose a calendar built anew.

sentences.zh: 謹立改易之意有二，設法之情有三。

translations.literal: I respectfully set forth two intentions for change and three points in establishing the method.
translations.idiomatic: My proposal rests on two principles of reform and three foundations for the new method.

sentences.zh: 改易者，其一，以舊法一章十九歲有七閏，閏數為多，經二百年，輒差一日。

translations.literal: Of the changes: the first—under the old method one chapter of nineteen years had seven intercalations; the number of intercalations was too great, and after two hundred years the calendar would be off by a day.
translations.idiomatic: First change: the old rule of seven leap months in nineteen years packs in too many intercalations—after two centuries the calendar slips a full day.

sentences.zh: 節閏既移，則應改法，曆紀屢遷，實由此條。

translations.literal: When nodes and intercalations shift, the method ought to be changed; the repeated migration of calendar eras stems in truth from this clause.
translations.idiomatic: When the leap-month cycle drifts, the method must change—and this, in truth, is why calendar eras keep being replaced.

sentences.zh: 今改章法，三百九十一年有一百四十四閏。

translations.literal: Now I change the intercalation rule: in three hundred ninety-one years there are one hundred forty-four intercalations.
translations.idiomatic: I propose instead 144 leap months in 391 years.

sentences.zh: 令卻合周、漢，則將來永用，無複差動。

translations.literal: Let it then accord with Zhou and Han, and in future it may be used forever without further drift.
translations.idiomatic: This aligns with Zhou and Han practice and should hold without further correction.

sentences.zh: 其二，以《堯典》雲：「日短星昴，以正仲冬。

translations.literal: Second: according to the Canon of Yao: "The days are short and the star is Mao; thereby fix mid-winter."
translations.idiomatic: Second change: the Canon of Yao says, "The days are short and the star Mao culminates—thereby fix mid-winter."

sentences.zh: 」以此推之，唐代冬至，日在今宿之左五十許度。

translations.literal: Pushing this forward, at the winter solstice of the Tang era the sun stood some fifty du to the left of its present lodge.
translations.idiomatic: By that reckoning, at the Tang-era winter solstice the sun stood some fifty du west of where it stands today.

sentences.zh: 漢代之初，即用秦曆，冬至日在牽牛六度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han they immediately used the Qin calendar; on the winter solstice the sun stood at Ox 6 du.
translations.idiomatic: At the Han founding the Qin calendar was still in use—the winter solstice sun at Ox 6 du.

sentences.zh: 漢武改立《太初曆》，冬至日在牛初。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han established the Taichu Calendar; on the winter solstice the sun stood at the head of Ox.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's Taichu Calendar placed the winter solstice at the head of Ox.

sentences.zh: 後漢《四分法》，冬至日在鬥二十二。

translations.literal: The Later Han Four Parts Calendar placed it at Dipper 22.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han Four Parts Calendar placed it at Dipper 22.

sentences.zh: 晉時薑岌以月蝕檢日，知冬至在鬥十七。

translations.literal: In Jin, Jiang Ji checked the day by lunar eclipse and knew the winter solstice stood at Dipper 17.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Jiang Ji verified by eclipse that the winter solstice stood at Dipper 17.

sentences.zh: 今參以中星，課以蝕望，冬至之日，在鬥十一。

translations.literal: Now, comparing midnight culminating stars and testing by eclipses and full moons, on the winter solstice the sun stands at Dipper 11.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing midnight stars with eclipses and syzygies, I find the winter solstice sun today at Dipper 11.

sentences.zh: 通而計之，未盈百載，所差二度。

translations.literal: Taken together and calculated, in less than a full century the discrepancy amounts to two du.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, in less than a century the solstice has drifted two du.

sentences.zh: 舊法並令冬至日有定處，天數既差，則七曜宿度漸與曆舛。

translations.literal: The old methods all fixed the winter solstice at a definite position; once the celestial numbers differ, the seven luminaries' lodge degrees gradually fall out of step with the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Old methods froze the solstice at a fixed lodge—but as the heavens move, the planets' positions slowly part company with the calendar.

sentences.zh: 乖謬既著，輒應改制，僅合一時，莫能通遠，遷革不已，又由此條。

translations.literal: Once the error is plain, the system ought to be changed; methods that barely fit one age cannot reach far; the endless succession of reforms stems again from this clause.
translations.idiomatic: Once the error shows, reform is inevitable; a calendar that barely fits one age cannot serve the long future—and this, too, is why systems are replaced again and again.

sentences.zh: 今令冬至所在，歲歲微差，卻檢漢注，並皆審密，將來久用，無煩屢改。

translations.literal: Now let the winter solstice position differ slightly year by year; checked against Han commentaries, all are exact—and in long use hereafter there will be no need for repeated change.
translations.idiomatic: Let the solstice advance slightly each year instead: checked against Han commentaries, the fit is exact, and the calendar should need no further overhaul.

sentences.zh: 又設法者，其一，以子為辰首，位在正北，爻應初九，鬥氣之端，虛為北方，列宿之中，元氣肇初，宜在此次。

translations.literal: Of the methods established: the first—take zi as the head of the double-hours, its position due north; the line corresponds to the first nine of the hexagrams; the Dipper marks the origin of qi; Emptiness is the center of the northern lodges; at the first origin of primal qi, the era ought to begin here.
translations.idiomatic: First foundation: take zi as the head of the double-hours at due north, matching the first nine of the hexagrams; the Dipper is the origin of celestial qi, Emptiness the hub of the northern lodges—the primal era should begin here.

sentences.zh: 前儒虞喜，備論其義。

translations.literal: The earlier scholar Yu Xi thoroughly discussed its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars—Yu Xi foremost among them—set out the full rationale.

sentences.zh: 今曆上元日度，發自虛一。

translations.literal: Now the calendar's upper-origin solar position begins from Emptiness 1.
translations.idiomatic: In the new calendar, the upper-origin solar longitude starts at Emptiness 1.

sentences.zh: 其二，以日辰之號，甲子為先，曆法設元，應在此歲。

translations.literal: Second: by the numbering of days and hours, jiazi comes first; in setting a calendar era, it should fall in this year.
translations.idiomatic: Second foundation: jiazi leads the sexagenary cycle—the calendar era ought to begin in that year.

sentences.zh: 而黃帝以來，世代所用，凡十一曆，上元之歲，莫值此名。

translations.literal: Yet from the Yellow Emperor down, through every age's usage—all eleven calendars—none placed the upper-origin year in jiazi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Yellow Emperor through eleven successive systems, not one upper-origin year has borne the name jiazi.

sentences.zh: 今曆上元，歲在甲子。

translations.literal: Now the calendar's upper origin falls in jiazi year.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar places its upper origin in a jiazi year.

sentences.zh: 其三，以上元之歲，曆中眾條，並應以此為始，而《景初曆》交會遲疾，亦置紀差，裁合朔氣而已。

translations.literal: Third: with the upper-origin year, every clause in the calendar ought to begin from it; yet the Jingchu Calendar's conjunction and slow-fast tables also set era offsets, barely aligning only new moons and qi.
translations.idiomatic: Third: every calendar procedure should start from the upper-origin year—but the Jingchu Calendar's eclipse and slow-fast tables still use era offsets, aligning new moons and qi and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 條序紛互，不及古意。

translations.literal: The clauses are tangled and jumbled, falling short of the ancient intent.
translations.idiomatic: Its procedures are tangled and jumbled—far from the older ideal.

sentences.zh: 今設法，日月五緯，交會遲疾，悉以上元歲首為始。

translations.literal: Now the method is set: sun, moon, five planets, conjunctions, slow and fast—all begin from the upper-origin year's head.
translations.idiomatic: Under my method, sun, moon, planets, eclipses, and slow-fast tables all originate at the upper-origin year.

sentences.zh: 則合璧之曜，信而有征，連珠之暉，於是乎在，群流共源，實精古法。

translations.literal: Then the paired-disk luminaries would be trusted and verified, the string-of-pearls radiance would be present; all streams share one source—truly refining the ancient method.
translations.idiomatic: Then the jade disks would align with proof, the pearls strung with light—and every strand of the calendar would share one spring, refining the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 若夫測以定形，據以實效，縣象著明，尺表之驗可推，動氣幽微，寸管之候不忒。

translations.literal: As for measuring to fix form, relying on real effect—the suspended images clear and bright, gnomon and rule can verify; the moving qi subtle, the inch-tube clepsydra's signs accurate.
translations.idiomatic: Measure form against fact: the sky's signs stand clear, gnomon shadows confirm it, and even the finest clepsydra pulse stays true.

sentences.zh: 今臣所立，易以取信。

translations.literal: What your subject has established is easy to trust.
translations.idiomatic: What I propose is easy to verify.

sentences.zh: 但深練始終，大存整密，革新變舊，有約有繁。

translations.literal: But practiced deep from start to finish, broadly preserved in integral precision—reforming the old, there are simplified and elaborate parts.
translations.idiomatic: It is painstaking from first principle to last, preserving whole precision while replacing the old—some steps spare, some elaborate.

sentences.zh: 用約之條，理不自懼，用繁之意，顧非謬然。

translations.literal: Using the simplified clauses, reason itself is not afraid; using the elaborate intent, surely it is not absurd.
translations.idiomatic: The simpler steps need no apology on grounds of logic; the more elaborate ones are not empty flourish.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why so?

sentences.zh: 夫紀閏參差，數各有分，分之為體，非細不密。

translations.literal: Era and intercalation vary by uneven amounts; each number has its fraction; fractions as the substance—without fineness there is no precision.
translations.idiomatic: Eras and leap months run on uneven fractions—without fine parts there is no real precision.

sentences.zh: 臣是用深惜毫釐，以全求妙之准，不辭積累，以成永定之制。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore deeply cherishes hairs and hairsbreadths to preserve the standard of seeking perfection, not shunning accumulation to forge a permanently fixed system.
translations.idiomatic: I weigh every hairbreadth to preserve exactness, and do not shirk the accumulation required for a lasting system.

sentences.zh: 非為思而莫悟，知而不改也，竊恐贊有然否，每崇遠而隨近；

translations.literal: It is not that one thinks and fails to grasp, or knows and does not change; I fear privately that supporters have their yes and no, always elevating what is distant and following what is near;
translations.idiomatic: This is not stubborn ignorance—I fear that reviewers honor what is near and dismiss what is far;

sentences.zh: 論有是非，或貴耳而遺目。

translations.literal: In debate there is right and wrong, or one values what is heard and neglects what is seen.
translations.idiomatic: Or trust what they hear and disregard what the eye can test.

sentences.zh: 所以竭其管穴，俯洗同異之嫌，披心日月，仰希葵藿之照。

translations.literal: Therefore I exhaust my narrow tube, bowing to wash away suspicion of difference; baring my heart to sun and moon, looking up to hope for the mallow's illumination.
translations.idiomatic: So I lay bare my narrow craft, hoping to clear every doubt—and offer my heart to sun and moon, as the mallow turns toward the light.

sentences.zh: 若臣所上，萬一可采，伏願頒宣群司，賜垂詳究，庶陳錙銖，少增盛典。

translations.literal: If what your subject submits might in the slightest be adopted, I humbly wish it promulgated to all offices, granted careful examination—perhaps this mite may slightly augment the great rite.
translations.idiomatic: If anything here may serve, I beg that it be sent to every office for review—even a grain might add something to the imperial rite.

sentences.zh: ○曆法

translations.literal: ○ Calendar method
translations.idiomatic: ○ Calendar Method

sentences.zh: 上元甲子至宋大明七年癸卯，五萬一千九百三十九年算外。

translations.literal: From upper origin jiazi to year gui-mao of Daming 7 in Song—51,939 years, outside the count.
translations.idiomatic: From the jiazi upper origin to Daming 7 (gui-mao): 51,939 years—exclusive of the count.

sentences.zh: 元法，五十九萬二千三百六十五。

translations.literal: Origin divisor: 592,365.
translations.idiomatic: Origin modulus (yuan fa): 592,365.

sentences.zh: 紀法，三萬九千四百九十一。

translations.literal: Era divisor: 39,491.
translations.idiomatic: Era modulus (ji fa): 39,491.

sentences.zh: 章歲，三百九十一。

translations.literal: Rule years: 391.
translations.idiomatic: Rule years (zhang sui): 391.

sentences.zh: 章月，四千八百三十六。

translations.literal: Rule months: 4,836.
translations.idiomatic: Rule months (zhang yue): 4,836.

sentences.zh: 章閏，一百四十四。

translations.literal: Rule intercalations: 144.
translations.idiomatic: Rule leap months (zhang run): 144.

sentences.zh: 閏法，十二。

translations.literal: Intercalation divisor: 12.
translations.idiomatic: Leap-month divisor (run fa): 12.

sentences.zh: 月法，十一萬六千三百二十一。

translations.literal: Month divisor: 116,321.
translations.idiomatic: Month modulus (yue fa): 116,321.

sentences.zh: 日法，三千九百三十九。

translations.literal: Day divisor: 3,939.
translations.idiomatic: Day modulus (ri fa): 3,939.

sentences.zh: 推朔術：置入上元年數，算外，以章月乘之，滿章歲為積月，不盡為閏餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing new moons: set the upper-origin year count outside the count; multiply by rule months; what fills rule years is accumulated months; what does not exhaust is intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To compute new moons: take years from the upper origin (exclusive), multiply by rule months (4,836), divide by rule years (391) for accumulated months; the remainder is the intercalary surplus.

sentences.zh: 閏餘二百四十七以上，其年有閏。

translations.literal: If the intercalary remainder is 247 or more, that year has an intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: If the intercalary remainder is 247 or greater, declare a leap month that year.

sentences.zh: 以月法乘積月，滿日法為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Multiply accumulated months by the month divisor; what fills the day divisor is accumulated days; what does not exhaust is small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply accumulated months by the month modulus (116,321), divide by the day modulus (3,939) for whole days; the residue is the fractional day.

sentences.zh: 六旬去積日，不盡為大餘。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what does not exhaust is great remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Strip full 60-day cycles from the day-count; the residue is the sexagenary day count.

sentences.zh: 大餘命以甲子，算外，所求年天正十一月朔也。

translations.literal: Name the great remainder from jiazi, outside the count—that is the new moon of Heaven's first month, month 11, of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Name the stem-branch date from jiazi (exclusive)—this gives the month-11 new moon of the target year.

sentences.zh: 小餘千八百四十九以上，其月大。

translations.literal: If the small remainder is 1,849 or more, that month is long.
translations.idiomatic: If the fractional remainder is 1,849 or greater, the month is a long (30-day) month.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加大餘二十九，小餘二千九十，小余滿日法從大余，大余滿六旬去之，命如前，次月朔也。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add twenty-nine to the great remainder and 2,090 to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry into the great remainder; when the great remainder fills six decades, remove it; name as before—that is the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month, add 29 days and 2,090 parts, carrying at the day modulus and stripping 60-day cycles—that yields the next new moon.

sentences.zh: 求弦望：加朔大餘七，小餘千五百七，小分一，小分滿四從小余，小余滿日法從大餘，命如前，上弦日也。

translations.literal: To seek first quarter and full moon: add seven to the new-moon great remainder, 1,507 to the small remainder, and one to the small fraction; when small fraction fills four, carry into small remainder; when small remainder fills the day divisor, carry into great remainder; name as before—that is the first-quarter day.
translations.idiomatic: For first quarter: add 7 days, 1,507 parts, and 1 small part to the new-moon date, carrying fractions as needed—that gives the first-quarter day.

sentences.zh: 又加得望，又加得下弦，又加得後月朔也。

translations.literal: Add again to obtain full moon; add again to obtain last quarter; add again to obtain the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the same addition for full moon, last quarter, and the following month's new moon.

sentences.zh: 推閏術：以閏余減章歲，余滿閏法得一月，命以天正，算外，閏所在也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing intercalary months: subtract rule years from the intercalary remainder; what fills the intercalation divisor gives one month; name from Heaven's first month, outside the count—the intercalation lies there.
translations.idiomatic: To locate the leap month: subtract 391 from the intercalary surplus, divide by 12; count forward from month 11—the leap month falls there.

sentences.zh: 閏有進退，以無中氣為正。

translations.literal: Intercalations may advance or retreat; govern them by the absence of a mid-term qi.
translations.idiomatic: Leap-month placement may shift; a month without a mid-climate qi must be intercalary.

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣術：置入上元年數，算外，以餘數乘之，滿紀法為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the twenty-four qi: set the upper-origin year count outside the count; multiply by the remainder number; what fills the era divisor is accumulated days; what does not exhaust is small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find the twenty-four solar terms: take years from the upper origin (exclusive), multiply by the remainder number (207,044), divide by the era modulus (39,491) for whole days; the residue is the fractional part.

sentences.zh: 六旬去積日，不盡為大餘。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what does not exhaust is great remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Remove 60-day cycles; the residue is the sexagenary day count.

sentences.zh: 大餘命以甲子，算外，天正十一月冬至日也。

translations.literal: Name the great remainder from jiazi, outside the count—that is the winter solstice day of Heaven's first month, month 11.
translations.idiomatic: Name the stem-branch date from jiazi (exclusive)—this is the month-11 winter solstice of the target year.

sentences.zh: 求次氣，加大餘十五，小餘八千六百二十六，小分五，小分滿六從小余，小余滿紀法從大餘，命如前，次氣日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next qi, add fifteen to the great remainder, 8,626 to the small remainder, and five to the small fraction; when small fraction fills six, carry into small remainder; when small remainder fills the era divisor, carry into great remainder; name as before—that is the next qi day.
translations.idiomatic: For the next term, add 15 days, 8,626 parts, and 5 small parts, carrying through the small-fraction, era, and sexagenary counts.

sentences.zh: 求土用事：加冬至大餘二十七，小余萬五千五百二十八，季冬土用事日也。

translations.literal: To seek Earth's reign: add twenty-seven to the winter-solstice great remainder and 15,528 to the small remainder—that is the late-winter day when Earth takes charge.
translations.idiomatic: For Earth's reign in late winter: add 27 days and 15,528 parts to the winter-solstice date.

sentences.zh: 又加大餘九十一，小余萬二千二百七十，次土用事日也。

translations.literal: Add again ninety-one to the great remainder and 12,270 to the small remainder—that is the next day when Earth takes charge.
translations.idiomatic: Add another 91 days and 12,270 parts for the second Earth-reign day.

sentences.zh: 推沒術：以九十乘冬至小餘，以減沒分，滿沒法為日，不盡為日餘，命日以冬至，算外，沒日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing extinction: multiply the winter-solstice small remainder by ninety and subtract from the extinction fraction; what fills the extinction divisor gives days; what does not exhaust is day remainder; name the day from the winter solstice, outside the count—that is the extinction day.
translations.idiomatic: For extinction days: multiply the winter-solstice fraction by 90, subtract from the extinction fraction (3,605,951), divide by the extinction divisor (51,761); name forward from the solstice.

sentences.zh: 求次沒，加日六十九，日余三萬四千四百四十二，余滿沒法從日，次沒日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next extinction, add sixty-nine days and day remainder 34,442; when the remainder fills the extinction divisor, carry into days—that is the next extinction day.
translations.idiomatic: For the following extinction, add 69 days and 34,442 parts, carrying at the extinction divisor.

sentences.zh: 日餘盡為滅。

translations.literal: When the day remainder is exhausted, it is an extinction day.
translations.idiomatic: When the day remainder reaches zero, that day is marked as extinction (mie).

sentences.zh: 推日所在度術：以紀法乘朔積日為度實，周天去之，余滿紀法為積度，不盡為度餘，命以虛一，次宿除之，算外，天正十一月朔夜半日所在度也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the sun's lodge degree: multiply new-moon accumulated days by the era divisor for degree dividend; remove circuit heaven; the remainder that fills the era divisor is accumulated degrees; what does not exhaust is degree remainder; name from Emptiness 1, remove lodges in sequence, outside the count—that is the sun's lodge degree at midnight on the month-11 new moon.
translations.idiomatic: For the sun's position at month-11 new-moon midnight: multiply accumulated days by the era modulus, reduce modulo circuit heaven, divide by the era modulus for whole degrees; name from Emptiness 1 and step through the lodges.

sentences.zh: 求次月，大月加度三十，小月加度二十九，入虛去度分。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add thirty degrees for a long month and twenty-nine for a short month; when entering Emptiness, remove the degree fraction.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month, add 30 du (long month) or 29 du (short month), applying the Emptiness-void correction to the fractional degree.

sentences.zh: 求行分，以小分法除度餘，所得為行分，不盡為小分。

translations.literal: To seek motion fen, divide the degree remainder by the small-fen divisor; what is obtained is motion fen; what is not exhausted is small fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Convert the degree remainder to motion fen by dividing by the small-fen divisor (1,717); the quotient is motion fen, the residue small parts.

sentences.zh: 小分滿法從行分，行分滿法從度。

translations.literal: When small fraction fills the divisor, carry into motion fen; when motion fen fills the divisor, carry into degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Carry small parts into motion fen and motion fen into whole degrees at their respective divisors.

sentences.zh: 求次日，加一度。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one degree.
translations.idiomatic: For the following day, add 1 du.

sentences.zh: 入虛去行分六，小分百四十七。

translations.literal: When entering Emptiness, remove six motion fen and 147 small parts.
translations.idiomatic: At Emptiness entry, subtract 6 motion fen and 147 small parts.

sentences.zh: 推月所在度術：以朔小餘乘百二十四為度餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the moon's lodge degree: multiply the new-moon small remainder by 124 for degree remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For the moon's position: multiply the new-moon fractional day by 124 for the degree remainder.

sentences.zh: 又以朔小餘乘八百六十為微分。

translations.literal: Again multiply the new-moon small remainder by 860 for micro-fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the same new-moon fraction by 860 for the micro-fraction.

sentences.zh: 微分滿月法從度余，度余滿紀法為度，以減朔夜半日所在，則月所在度。

translations.literal: When micro-fraction fills the month divisor, carry into degree remainder; when degree remainder fills the era divisor, form degrees; subtract from the new-moon midnight solar position—then the moon's lodge degree.
translations.idiomatic: Carry micro-parts into the degree remainder and then into whole degrees at the month and era moduli; subtract from the midnight solar longitude to obtain the moon's lodge.

sentences.zh: 求次月，大月加度三十五，度余三萬一千八百三十四，微分七萬七千九百六十七，小月加度二十二，度余萬七千二百六十一，微分六萬三千七百三十六，入虛去度分也。

translations.literal: To seek the next month: for a long month add thirty-five degrees, degree remainder 31,834, and micro-fraction 77,967; for a short month add twenty-two degrees, degree remainder 17,261, and micro-fraction 63,736; when entering Emptiness, remove the degree fraction.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 35 du (or 22 du for a short month) with the listed remainders and micro-parts, applying the Emptiness-void correction.
