sentences.zh: 推入遲疾曆術：以通法乘朔積日為通實，通周去之，余滿通法為日，不盡為日餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing entry into the slow-fast calendar: multiply new-moon accumulated days by the communication divisor for communication dividend; remove the communication circuit; the remainder that fills the communication divisor gives days; what does not exhaust is day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To enter the slow-fast table: multiply accumulated days by the communication divisor (26,377), reduce modulo the communication circuit (726,810); the quotient is whole days, the residue the fractional day.

sentences.zh: 命日算外，天正十一月朔夜半入曆日也。

translations.literal: Name the day outside the count—that is the slow-fast calendar-entry day at midnight on the month-11 new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Name the day count (exclusive)—this is the slow-fast index at month-11 new-moon midnight.

sentences.zh: 求次月，大月加二日，小月加一日，日余皆萬一千七百四十六。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add two days for a long month and one day for a short month; the day remainder is always 11,746.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 2 days (long) or 1 day (short), each with day remainder 11,746.

sentences.zh: 曆滿二十七日，日余萬四千六百三十一，則去之。

translations.literal: When the calendar fills twenty-seven days and the day remainder is 14,631, remove it.
translations.idiomatic: At the 27-day cycle limit, clear day remainder 14,631 and roll the table forward.

sentences.zh: 求次日，加一日。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one day.
translations.idiomatic: For the following day, add 1 day.

sentences.zh: 求日所在定度：以夜半入曆日餘乘損益率，以損益盈縮積分，如差率而一，所得滿紀法為度，不盡為度餘，以盈加縮減平行度及餘為定度。

translations.literal: To seek the corrected solar degree: multiply the midnight slow-fast calendar day remainder by the increase-decrease rate; by it increase or decrease the expansion-contraction accumulated parts; divide by the difference rate; what is obtained filling the era divisor is degrees; what does not exhaust is degree remainder; add for expansion and subtract for contraction from the mean degree and remainder for the corrected degree.
translations.idiomatic: For true solar longitude: scale the midnight table remainder by the rate, adjust the expansion-contraction integral, divide by the difference rate (39), carry at the era modulus, and add or subtract from the mean position.

sentences.zh: 益之或滿法，損之或不足，以紀法進退。

translations.literal: When increasing, it may fill the divisor; when decreasing, it may be insufficient—advance or retreat by the era divisor.
translations.idiomatic: If addition overflows or subtraction underflows, borrow or carry using the era modulus (39,491).

sentences.zh: 求度行分如上法。

translations.literal: To seek degree motion fen, use the method above.
translations.idiomatic: Convert the corrected degree remainder to motion fen by the same method as above.

sentences.zh: 求次日，如所入遲疾加之，虛去分如上法。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add according to the slow-fast entry as above; when entering Emptiness, remove fractions as above.

sentences.zh: 推入陰陽曆術：置通實以會周去之，不滿交數三十五萬八千八百八十八半為朔入陽曆分，滿去之，為朔入陰曆分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing entry into the yin-yang calendar: set the communication dividend; remove the conjunction circuit; what does not fill conjunction number 358,888½ is the new-moon entry into the yang-calendar fraction; when full remove it—for entry into the yin-calendar fraction.
translations.idiomatic: To enter the yin-yang table: take the communication dividend, reduce modulo the conjunction circuit (717,777); a remainder under the conjunction number (358,888½) is the yang fraction—otherwise subtract and take the yin fraction.

sentences.zh: 各滿通法得一日，不盡為日餘，命日算外，天正十一月朔夜半入曆日也。

translations.literal: Each, what fills the communication divisor gives one day; what is not exhausted is day remainder; name the day outside the count—that is the calendar-entry day at midnight on the month-11 new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Divide each fraction by the communication divisor (26,377) for whole days; name the day count (exclusive)—this is the yin-yang index at month-11 new-moon midnight.

sentences.zh: 求次月，大月加二日，小月加一日，日余皆二萬七百七十九。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add two days for a long month and one day for a short month; the day remainder is always 20,779.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 2 days (long) or 1 day (short), each with day remainder 20,779.

sentences.zh: 曆滿十三日，日余萬五千九百八十七半則去之。

translations.literal: When the calendar fills thirteen days and day remainder 15,987½, remove it.
translations.idiomatic: At the 13-day cycle limit, clear day remainder 15,987½ and roll the table forward.

sentences.zh: 陽竟入陰，陰竟入陽。

translations.literal: When yang ends, enter yin; when yin ends, enter yang.
translations.idiomatic: At yang cycle end, flip to yin—and vice versa.

sentences.zh: 求次日，加一日。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one day.
translations.idiomatic: For the following day, add 1 day.

sentences.zh: 求朔望差，以二千二十九乘朔小余，滿三百三為日餘，不盡倍之為小分，則朔差數也。

translations.literal: To seek new-moon and full-moon difference: multiply the new-moon small remainder by 2,029; what fills 303 becomes day remainder; what is not exhausted, double it for small fraction—that is the new-moon difference number.
translations.idiomatic: For the syzygy offset: multiply the new-moon fractional day by 2,029, divide by 303 for the day remainder, double the residue for small parts—that yields the new-moon difference index.

sentences.zh: 加一十四日，日余二萬一百八十六，小分百二十五，小分滿六百六從日余，日余滿通法為日，即望差數也。

translations.literal: Add fourteen days, day remainder 20,186, small fraction 125; when small fraction fills 606 carry into day remainder; when day remainder fills the communication divisor form days—that is the full-moon difference number.
translations.idiomatic: For full moon add 14 days, remainder 20,186, and small fraction 125, carrying at 606 and the communication divisor—that gives the full-moon difference index.

sentences.zh: 又加之，後月朔也。

translations.literal: Add again—that is the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the same addition for the following month's new moon.

sentences.zh: 求合朔月食：置朔望夜半入陰陽曆日及餘，有半者去之，置小分三百三，以差數加之，小分滿六百六從日余，日余滿通法從日，日滿一曆去之。

translations.literal: To seek conjunction and lunar eclipse: set the new-moon and full-moon midnight yin-yang calendar days and remainders; remove halves; set small fraction 303; add the difference number; when small fraction fills 606 carry into day remainder; when day remainder fills the communication divisor carry into days; when days fill one calendar remove it.
translations.idiomatic: For conjunction and lunar eclipse: take the midnight yin-yang index at syzygy, drop half-units, add small fraction 303 plus the difference index, carrying at 606 and 26,377 and clearing each 13-day table cycle.

sentences.zh: 命日算外，則朔望加時入曆也。

translations.literal: Name the day outside the count—that is the calendar entry at the hour of new moon and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: Name the day count (exclusive)—this is the yin-yang index at syzygy hour.

sentences.zh: 朔望加時入曆一日，日餘四千一百九十八，小分四百二十八以下，十二日，日余萬一千七百八十八，小分四百八十一以上，朔則交會，望則月食。

translations.literal: When new-moon and full-moon hour calendar entry is day one, day remainder 4,198, small fraction 428 or below—or day twelve, day remainder 11,788, small fraction 481 or above—at new moon there is conjunction, at full moon lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If the syzygy-hour index is day 1 (remainder ≤4,198, small fraction ≤428) or day 12 (remainder ≥11,788, small fraction ≥481), new moon brings conjunction and full moon brings lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 求合朔月食定大小餘：令差數日餘加夜半入遲疾曆余，日余滿通法從日，則朔望加時入曆也。

translations.literal: To seek the fixed great and small remainders for conjunction and lunar eclipse: let the difference-number day remainder add to the midnight slow-fast calendar remainder; when day remainder fills the communication divisor carry into days—that is the calendar entry at syzygy hour.
translations.idiomatic: To fix syzygy remainder: add the difference day-fraction to the midnight slow-fast remainder, carrying at the communication divisor—that yields the syzygy-hour table index.

sentences.zh: 以入曆餘乘損益率，以損益盈縮積分，如差法而一，以盈減縮加本朔望小餘，為定小餘。

translations.literal: Multiply the calendar-entry remainder by the increase-decrease rate; by it increase or decrease the expansion-contraction accumulated parts; divide by the difference divisor; surplus subtract, deficit add to the original new-moon and full-moon small remainder—for the fixed small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Scale the table remainder by the surplus-deficit rate, adjust the expansion-contraction integral, divide by the difference divisor, and subtract surplus or add deficit from the mean syzygy fraction for the true small remainder.

sentences.zh: 益之或滿法，損之或不足，以日法進退日。

translations.literal: When increasing it may fill the divisor; when decreasing it may be insufficient—advance or retreat the day by the day divisor.
translations.idiomatic: If addition overflows or subtraction underflows, borrow or carry a day using the day modulus (3,939).

sentences.zh: 求合朔月食加時：以十二乘定小余，滿日法得一辰，命以子，算外，加時所在辰也。

translations.literal: To seek the hour of conjunction and lunar eclipse: multiply the fixed small remainder by twelve; what fills the day divisor gives one double-hour; name from zi, outside the count—the double-hour where the addition falls.
translations.idiomatic: For syzygy hour: multiply the true fractional day by 12, divide by the day modulus (3,939), and name the stem-branch hour from zi (exclusive).

sentences.zh: 有餘者四之，滿日法得一為少，二為半，三為太。

translations.literal: If there is remainder, multiply by four; what fills the day divisor gives one as shao, two as ban, three as tai.
translations.idiomatic: For the leftover fraction, multiply by 4 and divide by the day modulus—1 gives shao (less), 2 ban (half), 3 tai (greater).

sentences.zh: 又有餘者三之，滿日法得一為強，以強並少為少強，並半為半強，並太為太強。

translations.literal: If there is still remainder, multiply by three; what fills the day divisor gives one as qiang; combine qiang with shao for shao-qiang, with ban for ban-qiang, with tai for tai-qiang.
translations.idiomatic: If fraction remains, multiply by 3 and divide by the day modulus—1 gives qiang (strong); combine with shao, ban, or tai for shao-qiang, ban-qiang, or tai-qiang.

sentences.zh: 得二者為少弱，以並太為一辰弱，以前辰名之。

translations.literal: Obtaining two gives shao-ruo; combine with tai for one double-hour weak; name by the prior double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Two qiang yields shao-ruo (less-weak); tai plus two qiang makes one chronogram weak—name the hour from the preceding stem-branch.

sentences.zh: 求月去日道度：置入陰陽曆餘乘損益率，如通法而一，以損益兼數為定，定數十二而一為度，不盡三而一，為少、半、太。

translations.literal: To seek the moon's distance from the sun's path in du: set the yin-yang calendar remainder; multiply by the increase-decrease rate; divide by the communication divisor; by it increase or decrease the combined number for the fixed value; divide the fixed number by twelve for du; what is not exhausted, divide by three for shao, ban, tai.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar latitude: multiply the yin-yang remainder by the surplus-deficit rate, divide by the communication divisor (26,377), adjust the paired number, divide by 12 for whole degrees, and express the remainder in thirds as shao, ban, or tai.

sentences.zh: 又不盡者，一為強，二為少弱，則月去日道數也。

translations.literal: What is still not exhausted—one gives qiang, two gives shao-ruo—that is the moon's distance from the sun's path number.
translations.idiomatic: Mark any leftover third as qiang (1) or shao-ruo (2)—the moon's ecliptic latitude.

sentences.zh: 陽曆在表，陰曆在裏。

translations.literal: The yang calendar is outside, the yin calendar inside.
translations.idiomatic: Yang-table latitude is north of the ecliptic; yin-table latitude is south.

sentences.zh: 求昏明中星：各以度數加夜半日所在，則中星度也。

translations.literal: To seek the dusk and dawn culminating stars: for each add the degree number to where the sun stands at midnight—that is the culminating-star degree.
translations.idiomatic: For dusk and dawn stars: add the tabulated arc to the midnight solar longitude to obtain the culminating-star position.

translations.idiomatic: For each planet: take the degree dividend (accumulated days × era modulus), divide by the orbital rate, subtract the remainder from the rate, divide again by the era modulus (39,491) for conjunction days—the residue is the fractional day.

sentences.zh: 命以天正朔，算外，星合日。

translations.literal: Name from Heaven's first-month new moon, outside the count—the star-conjunction day.
translations.idiomatic: Name the date forward from the month-11 new moon (exclusive)—the planetary conjunction day.

sentences.zh: 求星合度：以入歲日及餘從天正朔日積度及余，滿紀法從度，滿三百六十餘度分則去之，命以虛一，算外，星合所在度也。

translations.literal: To seek star-conjunction degree: add entry-year days and remainder to the first-month new-moon accumulated solar degree and remainder; when it fills the era modulus carry into du; when it fills 360 remove the degree fraction; name from Emptiness 1, outside the count—the degree where the star conjoins.
translations.idiomatic: For conjunction longitude: add the entry days and fraction to the month-11 new-moon solar position, carrying at the era modulus and stripping 360°, then name from Emptiness 1 (exclusive).

sentences.zh: 求星見日術：以伏日及餘，加星合日及余，余滿紀法從日，命如前，見日也。

translations.literal: Method for finding star-appearance day: add occultation days and remainder to star-conjunction day and remainder; when remainder fills the era modulus carry into days; name as before—the appearance day.
translations.idiomatic: For first visibility: add the tabulated occultation interval to the conjunction date, carrying at the era modulus, and name the date as before.

sentences.zh: 求星見度術：以伏度及餘，加星合度及余，余滿紀法從度，入虛去度分，命如前，星見度也。

translations.literal: Method for finding star-appearance degree: add occultation du and remainder to star-conjunction du and remainder; when remainder fills the era modulus carry into du; entering Emptiness remove degree fraction; name as before—the star-appearance degree.
translations.idiomatic: For appearance longitude: add the occultation arc to the conjunction position, carrying at the era modulus and applying the Emptiness-void correction, then name as before.

sentences.zh: 行五星法：以小分法除度餘，所得為行分，不盡為小分，及日加所行分滿法從度，留者因前，逆則減之，伏不盡度。

translations.literal: Method for moving the five planets: divide degree remainder by the small-fraction divisor; what is obtained is motion fen; what is not exhausted is small fraction; daily add the motion fen—when it fills the divisor carry into du; during stationary continue the prior value; in retrograde subtract; during occultation do not complete du.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the degree remainder by the small-fen divisor (1,717) for daily motion fen; add each day and carry into whole du; hold through stations, subtract in retrograde, and omit degrees while hidden.

sentences.zh: 從行入虛，去行分六，小分百四十七；

translations.idiomatic: At Emptiness entry in direct motion, subtract 6 motion fen and 147 small parts;

sentences.zh: 從，疾，日行一度五分，九十二日，行百十二度。

translations.literal: Direct, fast: daily motion one du five fen, 92 days, motion 112 du.
translations.idiomatic: Evening star direct fast phase: 1 du 5 fen per day for 92 days—112 du of travel.

sentences.zh: 小遲，日行一度四分，九十二日，行百八度。

translations.literal: Slightly slow: daily motion one du four fen, 92 days, motion 108 du.
translations.idiomatic: Evening star slightly slow phase: 1 du 4 fen per day for 92 days—108 du of travel.

sentences.zh: 大遲，日行十七分，四十五日，行三十三度六分。

translations.literal: Greatly slow: daily motion seventeen fen, 45 days, motion 33 du six fen.
translations.idiomatic: Evening star greatly slow phase: 17 fen per day for 45 days—33 du 6 fen of travel.

sentences.zh: 留九日。

translations.literal: Stationary nine days.
translations.idiomatic: It stations 9 days.

sentences.zh: 遲，日行十六分，退六度六分。

translations.literal: Slow: daily motion sixteen fen, retreat six du six fen.
translations.idiomatic: Slow retrograde at 16 fen per day—retreat 6 du 6 fen.

sentences.zh: 夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Evening hidden in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 伏五日，退五度，而與日合。

translations.literal: Occultation five days, retreat five du, then conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden 5 days, retreating 5 du, then conjoins with the sun.

sentences.zh: 又五日退五度，而晨見東方。

translations.literal: Again five days, retreat five du, then morning appearance in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden another 5 days, retreating 5 du, then appears in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 逆，日行十六分，九日。

translations.literal: Retrograde: daily motion sixteen fen, nine days.
translations.idiomatic: Morning star retrograde at 16 fen per day for 9 days.

sentences.zh: 留九日。

translations.literal: Stationary nine days.
translations.idiomatic: It stations 9 days.

sentences.zh: 從，遲，日行十七分，四十五日。

translations.literal: Direct, slow: daily motion seventeen fen, 45 days.
translations.idiomatic: Morning star direct slow phase: 17 fen per day for 45 days.

sentences.zh: 小疾，日行一度四分，九十二日。

translations.literal: Slightly fast: daily motion one du four fen, 92 days.
translations.idiomatic: Morning star slightly fast phase: 1 du 4 fen per day for 92 days.

sentences.zh: 大疾，日行一度五分，九十二日，晨伏東方，日度余如初。

translations.literal: Greatly fast: daily motion one du five fen, 92 days; morning hidden in the east; day and degree remainders as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Morning star greatly fast phase: 1 du 5 fen per day for 92 days, then hidden in the east at dawn; day and degree remainders return to their initial values.

sentences.zh: 一終，五百八十三日，日余三萬六千七百六十一，行星如之。

translations.literal: One cycle: 583 days, day remainder 36,761; planetary motion likewise.
translations.idiomatic: One complete cycle: 583 days (remainder 36,761); gross planetary motion matches.

sentences.zh: 除一周，定行二百十八度，度余二萬六千三百一十二。

translations.literal: Remove one circuit; net motion 218 du, degree remainder 26,312.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract one 360° circuit; net motion 218 du (remainder 26,312).

sentences.zh: 一合，二百九十一日，日余三萬八千一百二十六，行星亦如之。

translations.literal: One conjunction: 291 days, day remainder 38,126; planetary motion likewise.
translations.idiomatic: One conjunction period: 291 days (remainder 38,126); gross planetary motion matches.

sentences.zh: 水：初與日合，伏，十四日，日余三萬七千一百十五，行三十度，度余三萬七千一百一十五，夕見西方。

translations.literal: Water: at first conjunction with the sun, occultation fourteen days, day remainder 37,115, motion 30 du, degree remainder 37,115; evening appearance in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Water: after initial conjunction it is hidden 14 days (day remainder 37,115), moves 30 du (remainder 37,115), then appears in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 從，疾，日行一度六分，二十三日，行二十九度。

translations.literal: Direct, fast: daily motion one du six fen, 23 days, motion 29 du.
translations.idiomatic: Evening star direct fast phase: 1 du 6 fen per day for 23 days—29 du of travel.

sentences.zh: 遲，日行二十分，八日，行六度二十二分。

translations.literal: Slow: daily motion twenty fen, eight days, motion six du twenty-two fen.
translations.idiomatic: Evening star slow phase: 20 fen per day for 8 days—6 du 22 fen of travel.

sentences.zh: 留二日。

translations.literal: Stationary two days.
translations.idiomatic: It stations 2 days.

sentences.zh: 遲，日行十一分，二日，退二十二分。

translations.literal: Slow: daily motion eleven fen, two days, retreat twenty-two fen.
translations.idiomatic: Slow retrograde at 11 fen per day for 2 days—retreat 22 fen.

sentences.zh: 夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Evening hidden in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 伏八日，退八度，而與日合。

translations.literal: Occultation eight days, retreat eight du, then conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden 8 days, retreating 8 du, then conjoins with the sun.

sentences.zh: 又八日，退八度，晨見東方。

translations.literal: Again eight days, retreat eight du, then morning appearance in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden another 8 days, retreating 8 du, then appears in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 逆，日行十一分，二日。

translations.literal: Retrograde: daily motion eleven fen, two days.
translations.idiomatic: Morning star retrograde at 11 fen per day for 2 days.

sentences.zh: 留二日。

translations.literal: Stationary two days.
translations.idiomatic: It stations 2 days.

sentences.zh: 從，遲，日行二十分，八日。

translations.literal: Direct, slow: daily motion twenty fen, eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Morning star direct slow phase: 20 fen per day for 8 days.

sentences.zh: 疾，日行一度六分，二十三日，晨伏東方，日度余如初。

translations.literal: Fast: daily motion one du six fen, 23 days; morning hidden in the east; day and degree remainders as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Morning star fast phase: 1 du 6 fen per day for 23 days, then hidden in the east at dawn; day and degree remainders return to their initial values.

sentences.zh: 一終，百一十五日，日余三萬四千七百三十九，行星如之。

translations.literal: One cycle: 115 days, day remainder 34,739; planetary motion likewise.
translations.idiomatic: One complete cycle: 115 days (remainder 34,739); gross planetary motion matches.

sentences.zh: 一合，五十七日，日余三萬七千一百一十五，行星亦如之。

translations.literal: One conjunction: fifty-seven days, day remainder 37,115; planetary motion likewise.
translations.idiomatic: One conjunction period: 57 days (remainder 37,115); gross planetary motion matches.

sentences.zh: 上元之歲，歲在甲子，天正甲子朔夜半冬至，日月五星，聚于虛度之初，陰陽遲疾，並自此始。

translations.literal: In the upper-origin year, the year is in jiazi; Heaven's first month, jiazi new moon at midnight is winter solstice; sun, moon, and five stars gather at the start of Emptiness; yin-yang and slow-fast all begin from this point.
translations.idiomatic: At the upper origin (jiazi year), month-11 new-moon midnight is winter solstice; the sun, moon, and five planets align at Emptiness 1°—the yin-yang and slow-fast tables all start there.

sentences.zh: 世祖下之有司，使內外博議，時人少解歷數，竟無異同之辨。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ordered the relevant offices to have inner and outer circles debate broadly; few of the time understood calendrics, and in the end there was no argument of agreement or disagreement.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu ordered a broad review; few officials understood calendrics, and no real consensus emerged.

sentences.zh: 唯太子旅賁中郎將戴法興議，以為：

translations.literal: Only Palace Attendant Crown Prince Guard Central Commander Dai Fazxing argued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Only Dai Fazxing, Central Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard, submitted objections:

sentences.zh: 三精數微，五緯會始，自非深推測，窮識晷變，豈能刊古革今，轉正圭宿。

translations.literal: The three luminaries' numbers are subtle, the five planets' conjunction is the beginning; unless one deeply calculates and fully knows gnomon changes, how can one revise the ancients and change the present, turning and correcting the standard lodges?
translations.idiomatic: The motions of sun, moon, and planets are subtle; without deep calculation and mastery of gnomon variation, no one should revise ancient norms and reset the lodge system.

sentences.zh: 案沖之所議，每有違舛，竊以愚見，隨事辨問。

translations.literal: Examining what Chongzhi proposed, each point has errors; I venture my humble view and question each item in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi's proposals contain repeated errors; I offer these modest objections point by point.

sentences.zh: 案沖之新推曆術，「今冬至所在，歲歲微差」。

translations.literal: Examining Chongzhi's newly calculated calendar method: "now the winter-solstice position shifts slightly year by year."
translations.idiomatic: His new method claims "the winter-solstice position shifts slightly each year."

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：夫二至發斂，南北之極，日有恆度，而宿無改位。

translations.literal: Minister Fazxing argued: The two solstices mark expansion and contraction, the poles of north and south; the sun has a fixed degree-span, but the lodges do not change position.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing argued: The solstices mark the sun's fixed limits; though it travels a constant arc, the lodges do not shift.

sentences.zh: 古曆冬至，皆在建星。

translations.literal: In ancient calendars, winter solstice was always at Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient calendars all placed winter solstice at Jian.

sentences.zh: 戰國橫騖，史官喪紀，爰及漢初，格候莫審，後雜覘知在南斗二十二度，元和所用，即與古曆相符也。

translations.literal: During the Warring States' chaos, historians lost the records; down to early Han, the frame-measures were unsure; later mixed observation placed it at Nan-dou 22°, and the Yuanhe calendar used this—which matched the ancient calendar.
translations.idiomatic: After Warring States chaos and lost records, early Han measurements were uncertain; later observation found winter solstice at Nan-dou 22°, which Yuanhe adopted—matching antiquity.

sentences.zh: 逮至景初，而終無毫忒。

translations.literal: Down to Jingchu, there was not a hair's error in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Jingchu calendar, not a hair's-breadth of error remained.

sentences.zh: 《書》雲：「日短星昴，以正仲冬。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "The day is short and the Mao stars are up, to rectify mid-winter.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents states: "The day is short and Mao culminates—this fixes mid-winter.

sentences.zh: 」直以月維四仲，則中宿常在衛陽，羲、和所以正時，取其萬世不易也。

translations.literal: "Simply by the moon's axis at the four mid-seasons, the central lodges are always in Wei and Yang; Xi and He rectified time by this, taking its unchanging through ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Xi and He fixed time by the four mid-season lunar axes with central stars in Wei and Yang—a standard meant to endure forever."

sentences.zh: 沖之以為唐代冬至日在今宿之左五十許度，遂虛加度分，空撤天路。

translations.literal: Chongzhi thinks the Tang-era winter solstice was about fifty degrees to the left of today's lodges, and thus vainly adds degrees, emptying and removing the heavenly path.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi places Tang-era winter solstice fifty degrees west of today's lodges—artificially adding arc and erasing the celestial path.

sentences.zh: 其置法所在，近違半次，則四十五年九月，率移一度。

translations.literal: Where his method sets its position, it nearly deviates half a lodge; then every forty-five years and nine months, on average it shifts one degree.
translations.idiomatic: His method deviates nearly half a lodge; solstice position would drift one degree every ~46 years.

sentences.zh: 在《詩》「七月流火」，此夏正建申之時也。

translations.literal: In the Odes, "In the seventh month the Fire streams west"—this is when the Xia calendar sets its first month at jian-shen.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes' "In the seventh month the Fire streams west" marks the Xia first month (jian-shen).

sentences.zh: 「定之方中」，又小雪之節也。

translations.literal: "'Ding establishes the center' is also the Lesser Snow solar term."
translations.idiomatic: "'Ding establishes the center' corresponds to Lesser Snow."

sentences.zh: 若冬至審差，則豳公火流，晷長一尺五寸，楚宮之作，晝漏五十三刻，此詭之甚也。

translations.literal: If winter solstice truly differed, then the Duke of Bin's Fire-streaming would give a gnomon shadow of one chi five cun, and the Chu palace construction would give a day clepsydra of fifty-three marks—this is utterly absurd.
translations.idiomatic: If solstice really shifted, Bin's Fire would imply a 1.5-chi shadow and Chu's palace a 53-mark day clepsydra—absurd implications.

sentences.zh: 仲尼曰：「丘聞之，火伏而後蟄者畢。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "I have heard that after the Fire sets, the hibernators finish.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "After Antares sets, all creatures finish hibernating.

sentences.zh: 今火猶西流，司曆過也。

translations.literal: Now the Fire still streams west—the calendar officer is at fault."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Fire still streams west—the calendar is off."

sentences.zh: 」就如沖之所誤，則星無定次，封有差方。

translations.literal: If as Chongzhi's error holds, then stars have no fixed order and domains have differing directions.
translations.idiomatic: On Zu Chongzhi's view, stars lack fixed order and the realm's cardinal directions would shift.

sentences.zh: 名號之正，古今必殊，典誥之音，代不通軌，堯之開、閉，今成建、除。

translations.literal: The correctness of names and titles must differ past and present; the sounds of canonical edicts cannot match across ages; Yao's "open" and "close" would become today's "establish" and "remove."
translations.idiomatic: Proper names would change with every age; Yao's calendar terms would become today's jian and chu.

sentences.zh: 今之壽星，乃周之鶉尾，即時東壁，已非玄武，軫星頓屬蒼龍，誣天痛經，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Today's Longevity Star is actually Zhou's Chimei; at present Eastern Wall is no longer Black Tortoise, and Zhen suddenly belongs to Azure Dragon—blaspheming Heaven and violating the classics, it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Longevity Star would be Zhou's Chimei; Eastern Wall would leave Black Tortoise and Zhen join Azure Dragon—blasphemy against Heaven and the classics.

sentences.zh: 沖之又改章法三百九十一年有一百四十四閏。

translations.literal: Chongzhi also changed the rule to 144 intercalations in 391 years.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi also replaces the intercalation rule with 144 leap months in 391 years.

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：夫日有緩急，故鬥有闊狹，古人制章，立為中格，年積十九，常有七閏，晷或虛盈，此不可革。

translations.literal: Minister Fazxing argued: Days have slow and fast phases, so the Dipper's span has wide and narrow; ancients made rules and set a middle standard—nineteen years accumulated always have seven intercalations; gnomon shadow may be empty or full—this cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing argued: Days vary in length, so the Dipper's span varies; the 19-year/7-leap rule with its gnomon tolerance must not be altered.

sentences.zh: 沖之削閏壞章，倍減餘數，則一百三十九年二月，於四分之科，頓少一日；

translations.literal: Chongzhi cuts intercalations and ruins the rule, halving the remainders; then in 139 years, in the second month, under the Quarter-day system one day is suddenly lost;
translations.idiomatic: Halving the intercalary remainder loses a full day in month 2 of year 139 under the Quarter-day schema.

sentences.zh: 七千四百二十九年，輒失一閏。

translations.literal: In 7,429 years, one intercalation is lost each time.
translations.idiomatic: Every 7,429 years one entire leap month is lost.

sentences.zh: 夫日少則先時，閏失則事悖。

translations.literal: When days are too few, times come early; when intercalations are lost, affairs go wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Too few days means early seasons; a missing leap month disrupts the calendar.

sentences.zh: 竊聞時以作事，事以厚生，以此乃生人之大本，歷數之所先，愚恐非沖之淺慮妄可穿鑿。

translations.literal: I have heard that seasons govern work, work nourishes life—this is the great foundation of human existence and what calendrics must put first; I fear Chongzhi's shallow thinking should not rashly be forced through.
translations.idiomatic: Calendrics underpin agriculture and human life; I doubt Zu Chongzhi's shallow reasoning should be imposed by force.

sentences.zh: 沖之又命上元日度發自虛一，雲虛為北方列宿之中。

translations.literal: Chongzhi also orders the upper-origin solar degree to start from Emptiness 1, saying Emptiness is the center of the northern lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi also starts the upper origin at Emptiness 1°, calling Xu the midpoint of the northern lodges.

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：沖之既雲冬至歲差，又謂虛為北中，舍形責影，未足為迷。

translations.literal: Minister Fazxing argued: Chongzhi both says winter solstice has annual precession and says Emptiness is northern center—abandoning form and blaming shadow is not enough to count as error.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing argued: Zu Chongzhi claims precession yet makes Xu the north center—relying on shadow over form is not necessarily wrong.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 凡在天非日不明，居地以鬥而辨。

translations.literal: Generally in the heavens nothing is clear without the sun; on earth one distinguishes by the Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In the sky nothing is visible without the sun; on earth we orient by the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 借令冬至在虛，則黃道彌遠，東北當為黃鐘之宮，室壁應屬玄枵之位，虛宿豈得複為北中乎？

translations.literal: Suppose winter solstice were at Emptiness: then the ecliptic would be far removed; northeast should be the Yellow Bell palace, Room and Wall should belong to Dark Arc positions—how can Emptiness again be northern center?
translations.idiomatic: If solstice were at Xu, the ecliptic would be displaced: Room and Wall would belong to Dark Arc, and Xu could hardly remain the north center.

sentences.zh: 曲使分至屢遷，而星次不改，招搖易繩，而律呂仍往，則七政不以璣衡致齊，建時亦非攝提所紀，不知五行何居，六屬安托？

translations.literal: Forcing solstices and equinoxes to shift repeatedly while star order does not change, changing the Dipper's plumb-line while pitch-pipes stay the same—then the seven regulators would not be aligned by the armillary, and establishment of time would not be recorded by Sheti; who knows where the Five Phases reside and what the six categories attach to?
translations.idiomatic: Forcing equinoxes to drift while lodges stay fixed—and shifting the Dipper while pitch-pipes stay put—would break armillary alignment, Sheti reckoning, and the placement of the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 沖之又令上元年在甲子。

translations.literal: Chongzhi also sets the upper-origin year in jiazi.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi also places the upper origin in a jiazi year.

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：夫置元設紀，各有所尚，或據文於圖讖，或取效於當時。

translations.literal: Minister Fazxing argued: Setting origin and establishing era each has its preference—some rely on texts in apocrypha, some take effect from the present age.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing argued: Every calendar picks its origin differently—some follow apocrypha, some fit contemporary observation.

sentences.zh: 沖之雲，「群氏糾紛，莫審其會」。

translations.literal: Chongzhi says: "Schools dispute, none can ascertain the conjunction."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi himself wrote: "Schools dispute—none can fix the conjunction."

sentences.zh: 昔《黃帝》辛卯，日月不過；

translations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor calendar: xinmao—sun and moon never exceeded;
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor calendar (xinmao): sun and moon never missed;

sentences.zh: 《顓頊》乙卯，四時不忒；

translations.literal: Zhuanxu: yimao—four seasons without error;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuanxu calendar (yimao): the four seasons never err;

sentences.zh: 《景初》壬辰，晦無差光；

translations.literal: Jingchu: renchen—last day of month without error in brightness;
translations.idiomatic: The Jingchu calendar (renchen): month-ends never miss;

sentences.zh: 《元嘉》庚辰，朔無錯景，豈非承天者乎！

translations.literal: Yuanjia: gengchen—new moon without wrong shadow—are these not heaven-compliant?
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanjia calendar (gengchen): new moons never misfire—true heaven-compliant calendars!

sentences.zh: 沖之苟存甲子，可謂為合以求天也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi merely keeps jiazi—this can be called conforming to fit heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi merely picks jiazi—fitting the numbers to please heaven.

sentences.zh: 沖之又令日月五緯，交會遲疾，悉以上元為始。

translations.literal: Chongzhi also sets sun, moon, five planets, conjunctions, slow-fast—all to start from the upper origin.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi also resets sun, moon, planets, syzygies, and slow-fast tables all from the upper origin.

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：夫交會之元，則食既可求，遲疾之際，非凡夫所測。

translations.literal: Minister Fazxing argued: The origin of conjunction—eclipses can be sought from it; the juncture of slow-fast is not what ordinary men can measure.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing argued: Conjunction origins predict eclipses; slow-fast cycles are beyond ordinary measurement.

sentences.zh: 昔賈逵略見其差，劉洪觕著其術。

translations.literal: Formerly Jia Kui briefly saw its discrepancy; Liu Hong roughly set forth its method.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui glimpsed the discrepancy; Liu Hong roughly codified the method.

sentences.zh: 至於疏密之數，莫究其極。

translations.literal: As for the numbers of density and sparsity, none have reached their limit.
translations.idiomatic: No one has fully resolved the dense and sparse parameters.

sentences.zh: 且五緯所居，有時盈縮，即如歲星在軫，見超七辰，術家既追算以會今，則往之與來，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the five planets' positions sometimes expand and contract; just as when Jupiter is at Zhen, its appearance exceeds seven lodges—if calendrists have already traced calculation to match the present, then past and future can surely be known.
translations.idiomatic: Planets expand and contract—for example Jupiter at Zhen leaps seven lodges; astronomers already project forward and back from the present.

sentences.zh: 《景初》所以紀首置差，《元嘉》兼又各設後元者，其並省功於實用，不虛推以為煩也。

translations.literal: Why Jingchu sets a difference at era-head and Yuanjia also each sets a later origin—they all economize effort for practical use, not pushing empty calculation for bother.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu and Yuanjia set era offsets and later origins to save effort—not to pile on useless calculation.

sentences.zh: 沖之既違天于改易，又設法以遂情，愚謂此治曆之大過也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi both violates heaven in reform and sets methods to suit his wishes—I deem this the great fault in governing calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi both defies heaven and bends rules to his wishes—the gravest fault in calendar reform.

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：日有八行，各成一道，月有一道，離為九行，左交右疾，倍半相違，其一終之理，日數宜同。

translations.literal: Minister Fazxing argued: The sun has eight paths, each forming one track; the moon has one path, divided into nine paths; left conjunction and right fast, double and half mutually differ—in the logic of one cycle, day numbers should be the same.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing argued: The sun has eight paths and the moon nine; left conjunction and right fast differ by halves—in one complete cycle their day counts should match.

sentences.zh: 沖之通周與會周相覺九千四十，其陰陽七十九周有奇，遲疾不及一匝。

translations.literal: Chongzhi's communication circuit and conjunction circuit differ by 9,040; his yin-yang is seventy-nine circuits plus a fraction; slow-fast falls short of one full turn.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi's communication and conjunction circuits differ by 9,040; yin-yang runs 79+ cycles while slow-fast falls short of one turn.

sentences.zh: 此則當縮反盈，應損更益。

translations.literal: This means what should shrink instead expands, what should decrease instead increases.
translations.idiomatic: Deficit becomes surplus and decrease becomes increase—the logic is inverted.

sentences.zh: 沖之隨法興所難辯折之曰：

translations.literal: Chongzhi, following Fazxing's objections, rebutted and refuted, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi answered Dai Fazxing's objections point by point:

sentences.zh: 臣少銳愚尚，專功數術，搜練古今，博采沈奧，唐篇夏典，莫不揆量，周正漢朔，鹹加該驗。

translations.literal: I from youth have been keen though foolish, devoted to numerology; I searched and refined past and present, broadly gathered hidden depths; Tang documents and Xia canon, none not weighed; Zhou new moons and Han first-of-month, all subjected to verification.
translations.idiomatic: From youth I devoted myself to mathematics, surveying Tang and Xia texts and verifying Zhou and Han new-moon records.

sentences.zh: 罄策籌之思，究疏密之辨。

translations.literal: I exhausted thought on reckoning and calculation, investigating the distinction of sparse and dense.
translations.idiomatic: I exhausted every reckoning to resolve dense and sparse parameters.

sentences.zh: 至若立圓舊誤，張衡述而弗改；

translations.literal: As for the old error in setting the circle, Zhang Heng transmitted it without correction;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng perpetuated the old sphere error without correction;

sentences.zh: 漢時斛銘，劉歆詭謬其數，此則算氏之劇疵也。

translations.literal: The Han-era hu inscription—Liu Xin perversely falsified its numbers; these are gross flaws of the calculators.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin's falsification of the Han hu inscription was a gross mathematical error.

sentences.zh: 《乾象》之弦望定數，《景初》之交度周日，匪謂測候不精，遂乃乘除翻謬，斯又曆家之甚失也。

translations.literal: Qianxiang's quarter-moon fixed numbers, Jingchu's crossing-degree circuit day—not that observation was imprecise, but multiplication and division were turned wrong; this again is calendrists' grave fault.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiang's syzygy constants and Jingchu's nodal month stem from botched arithmetic—not imprecise observation.

sentences.zh: 及鄭玄、闞澤、王蕃、劉徽，並綜數藝，而每多疏舛。

translations.literal: And Zheng Xuan, Kan Ze, Wang Fan, Liu Hui—all combined numerical arts, yet each has many gaps and errors.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan, Kan Ze, Wang Fan, and Liu Hui all compiled mathematical arts—yet each is riddled with errors.

sentences.zh: 臣昔以暇日，撰正眾謬，理據炳然，易可詳密，此臣以俯信偏識，不虛推古人者也。

translations.literal: I in past leisure days compiled corrections of many errors; reasoning and evidence are clear, easily made detailed and precise—this is because I humbly trust partial knowledge, not pushing empty credit on ancients.
translations.idiomatic: In past leisure I corrected many errors on clear evidence—I do not credit ancients blindly.

sentences.zh: 按何承天曆，二至先天，閏移一月，五星見伏，或違四旬，列差妄設，當益反損，皆前術之乖遠，臣曆所改定也。

translations.literal: Examining He Chengtian's calendar: solstices ahead of heaven, intercalation shifted a month, five stars' visibility and hiding sometimes off four ten-day weeks, column differences falsely set—should increase yet decrease—all departures of prior methods that my calendar has corrected.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's calendar put solstices early, misplaced leap months, and mis-timed planetary visibility—all corrected in my calendar.

sentences.zh: 既沿波以討其源，刪滯以暢其要，能使躔次上通，晷管下合，反以譏詆，不其惜乎！

translations.literal: Having traced the waves to seek the source, cut stagnation to clarify the essentials— able to make lodge positions accord above and gnomon-clepsydra accord below— yet instead to be slandered, is this not regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Having traced errors to their source and streamlined the method to unify lodge motion with gnomon and clepsydra, I am slandered instead—is that not regrettable?

sentences.zh: 尋法興所議六條，並不造理難之關楗。

translations.literal: Examining Fazxing's six debated points, none reaches the gate-bar of rational objection.
translations.idiomatic: None of Dai Fazxing's six objections reaches a substantive difficulty.

sentences.zh: 謹陳其目。

translations.literal: I respectfully set forth their headings.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully list them.

sentences.zh: 其一，日度歲差，前法所略，臣據經史辨正此數，而法興設難，徵引《詩》《書》，三事皆謬。

translations.literal: First: solar-degree annual precession—prior methods overlooked it; I corrected this number from classics and history, yet Fazxing raises difficulty citing Odes and Documents—all three points are wrong.
translations.idiomatic: First, precession: prior methods ignored it; Dai Fazxing's Odes and Documents citations on all three points are wrong.

sentences.zh: 其二，臣校晷景，改舊章法，法興立難，不能有詰，直雲「恐非淺慮，所可穿鑿」。

translations.literal: Second: I calibrated gnomon shadow and changed the old intercalation rule; Fazxing raised difficulty but could not interrogate, merely saying "I fear this is not shallow thinking that can be forced through."
translations.idiomatic: Second, intercalation: Dai Fazxing could only say "shallow thinking should not be forced through"—no substantive rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 其三，次改方移，臣無此法，求術意誤，橫生嫌貶。

translations.literal: Third: next, changing direction and shifting—I have no such method; he misread the method's intent and groundlessly raised suspicion and denigration.
translations.idiomatic: Third, he attacks a "direction shift" I never proposed—misreading my method.

sentences.zh: 其四，曆上元年甲子，術體明整，則苟合可疑。

translations.literal: Fourth: calendar upper origin in jiazi year—the method's structure is clear and whole, so he suspects forced fit.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, jiazi upper origin: because the method is coherent, he suspects forced fit.

sentences.zh: 其五，臣其曆七曜，鹹始上元，無隙可乘，複雲「非凡夫所測」。

translations.literal: Fifth: my calendar's seven luminaries all start from upper origin—no gap to exploit—yet he again says "not what ordinary men can measure."
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, syzygy tables from the upper origin leave no gap—yet he calls it "beyond ordinary measure."

sentences.zh: 其六，遲疾陰陽，法興所未解，誤謂兩率日數宜同。

translations.literal: Sixth: slow-fast and yin-yang—what Fazxing has not understood; he mistakenly thinks the two rates' day numbers should be the same.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, slow-fast and yin-yang: Dai Fazxing misunderstood them and wrongly demands equal day counts.

sentences.zh: 凡此眾條，或援謬目譏，或空加抑絕，未聞折正之談，厭心之論也。

translations.literal: All these many points—some cite errors to mock, some empty add suppression and rejection—never have I heard correcting discourse or discourse that satisfies the heart.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: mockery citing errors, or bare dismissal—never a fair rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 謹隨詰洗釋，依源征對。

translations.literal: I respectfully follow each query to clarify, according to source to verify and match.
translations.idiomatic: I respond to each point at its source.

sentences.zh: 仰照天暉，敢罄管穴。

translations.literal: Looking up to heaven's radiance, I dare exhaust my narrow insight.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly invoking heaven's light, I offer this narrow insight.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「夫二至發斂，南北之極，日有恆度，而宿無改位。

translations.literal: Fazxing argued: "The two solstices mark expansion and contraction, the poles of north and south; the sun has a fixed degree-span, but the lodges do not change position.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing restated: "The solstices mark fixed limits; the sun travels a constant arc but lodges do not shift.

sentences.zh: 故古曆冬至，皆在建星」。

translations.literal: Therefore ancient calendars' winter solstice was always at Jian."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore ancient calendars placed winter solstice at Jian."

sentences.zh: 沖之曰：周漢之際，疇人喪業，曲技競設，圖緯實繁，或借號帝王以崇其大，或假名聖賢以神其說。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: Between Zhou and Han, calendrists lost their profession; crooked techniques competed; apocrypha were abundant—some borrowed imperial titles to magnify themselves, some used sage names to sanctify their doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi replied: Between Zhou and Han calendrists lost their craft; apocrypha flourished, borrowing imperial and sage names to sanctify false claims.

sentences.zh: 是以讖記多虛，桓譚知其矯妄；

translations.literal: Thus prognostications were mostly empty—Huan Tan knew their falsity;
translations.idiomatic: Prognostications were mostly false—Huan Tan saw through them;

sentences.zh: 古曆舛雜，杜預疑其非直。

translations.literal: ancient calendars were mixed and wrong—Du Yu doubted their straightness.
translations.idiomatic: and ancient calendars were confused—Du Yu doubted their reliability.

sentences.zh: 按《五紀論》黃帝曆有四法，顓頊、夏、周並有二術，詭異紛然，則孰識其正，此古曆可疑之據一也。

translations.literal: Examining the Five Era Discourse: the Yellow Emperor calendar had four methods; Zhuanxu, Xia, and Zhou each had two techniques—contradictions abundant—who knows which is correct? This is grounds one for doubting ancient calendars.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Era Discourse lists four Yellow Emperor methods and duplicate Zhuanxu, Xia, and Zhou systems—who knows which is authentic? Ground one for doubt.

sentences.zh: 夏曆七曜西行，特違眾法，劉向以為後人所造，此可疑之據二也。

translations.literal: The Xia calendar's seven luminaries move west—specially violating common methods; Liu Xiang thought it was made by later men—grounds two for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia calendar's westward luminaries violate all other methods—Liu Xiang deemed it a later forgery. Ground two.

sentences.zh: 殷曆日法九百四十，而《乾鑿度》雲殷曆以八十一為日法。

translations.literal: The Yin calendar's day divisor is 940, yet Qianzaodu says the Yin calendar uses 81 as day divisor.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin day divisor is 940, yet Qianzaodu says 81.

sentences.zh: 若《易緯》非差，殷曆必妄，此可疑之據三也。

translations.literal: If the Changes apocryphon is not wrong, the Yin calendar must be false—grounds three for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If the apocryphon is wrong, the Yin calendar is fake. Ground three.

sentences.zh: 《顓頊》曆元，歲在乙卯，而《命曆序》雲：「此術設元，歲在甲寅。

translations.literal: The Zhuanxu calendar origin: year in yimao, yet the Command Calendar Preface says: "This method sets origin, year in jiayin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu sets its origin in yimao, yet Command Calendar Preface says jiayin.

sentences.zh: 」此可疑之據四也。

translations.literal: " This is grounds four for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Ground four for doubt.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》書食有日朔者凡二十六，其所據曆，非周則魯。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn records eclipses with day and new moon twenty-six in all; the calendar it relies on is either Zhou or Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn records 26 dated eclipses using either the Zhou or Lu calendar.

sentences.zh: 以周曆考之，檢其朔日，失二十五，魯曆校之，又失十三。

translations.literal: Testing with the Zhou calendar, checking its new-moon days—twenty-five failures; testing with the Lu calendar—thirteen more failures.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou calendar misses 25; the Lu calendar misses 13 more.

sentences.zh: 二曆並乖，則必有一偽，此可疑之據五也。

translations.literal: Both calendars are wrong—then one must be false; grounds five for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Both fail—one must be forged. Ground five.

sentences.zh: 古之六術，並同《四分》，《四分》之法，久則後天。

translations.literal: The ancient six methods all match the Quarter-day; the Quarter-day method, over time, falls behind heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The six ancient methods match the Quarter-day calendar, which drifts behind heaven over time.

sentences.zh: 以食檢之，經三百年，輒差一日。

translations.literal: Testing by eclipses, after three hundred years it errs one day.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse checks show ~1 day error every 300 years.

sentences.zh: 古曆課今，其甚疏者，朔後天過二日有餘。

translations.literal: Ancient calendars tested against today—the most lax ones, new moons fall behind heaven by more than two days.
translations.idiomatic: The worst ancient calendars put new moons 2+ days late against today.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，古術之作，皆在漢初週末，理不得遠。

translations.literal: From this inference, ancient methods' composition—all at end of Zhou and early Han; logically cannot be far back.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient methods were composed near the Han founding—logically not much earlier.

sentences.zh: 且卻校《春秋》，朔並先天，此則非三代以前之明征矣，此可疑之據六也。

translations.literal: Moreover checking Spring and Autumn backward, new moons all ahead of heaven—this is not clear evidence from before the Three Dynasties; grounds six for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Checked against Spring and Autumn, new moons are all early—not evidence from before the Three Dynasties. Ground six.

sentences.zh: 尋《律曆志》，前漢冬至日在鬥牛之際，度在建星，其勢相鄰，自非帝者有造，則儀漏或闕，豈能窮密盡微，纖毫不失。

translations.literal: Examining the Treatise on Pitchpipes and Calendrics: Former Han winter solstice was at the juncture of Dipper and Ox, degree at Jian—they are adjacent; unless the Emperor crafted it, then instruments and clepsydrae may have been lacking—how could it reach exhaustive fineness without a hair's loss?
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise places Former Han solstice between Dipper and Ox near Jian—only an imperial fabrication, or faulty instruments, could claim such precision.

sentences.zh: 建星之說，未足證矣。

translations.literal: The Jian-star claim is insufficient as proof.
translations.idiomatic: The Jian-star claim does not hold.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「戰國橫騖，史官喪紀，爰及漢初，格候莫審，後雜覘知在南斗二十二度，元和所用，即與古曆相符也。

translations.literal: Fazxing argued: "Warring States ran wild, historians lost records; down to early Han, frame-measures were unsure; later mixed observation placed it at Nan-dou 22°, Yuanhe used this—which matched the ancient calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing restated his Warring States chaos argument and Yuanhe's Nan-dou 22° placement.

sentences.zh: 逮至景初，終無毫忒。

translations.literal: Down to Jingchu, not a hair's error in the end."
translations.idiomatic: Through Jingchu, not a hair's error."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：古術訛雜，其詳闕聞，乙卯之曆，秦代所用，必有效於當時，故其言可征也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: Ancient methods are erroneous and mixed, details lost; the yimao calendar used in Qin must have been effective then, so its words can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi replied: ancient methods are confused; the Qin yimao calendar worked in its day—that is why its claims survive.

sentences.zh: 漢武改創，檢課詳備，正儀審漏，事在前史，測星辨度，理無乖遠。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu reformed and created; inspection was detailed and complete; corrected instruments and examined clepsydrae—matters are in prior histories; measuring stars and distinguishing degrees—logic has no gross departure.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wu's reforms were thoroughly tested; star measurement and degree reckoning are documented in prior histories without gross error.

sentences.zh: 今議者所是不實見，所非徒為虛妄，辨彼駭此，既非通談，運今背古，所誣誠多，偏據一說，未若兼今之為長也。

translations.literal: Now the debaters' affirmations are not real observation; their negations are merely empty falsehood; debating that to alarm this is not universal discourse; applying present to reject antiquity—the slanders are truly many; relying on one doctrine is not as good as combining present as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Today's debaters affirm without real evidence and deny without cause; rejecting the present to blindly follow antiquity slanders much truth—combining modern observation with ancient texts is better than clinging to one school.

sentences.zh: 《景初》之法，實錯五緯，今則在沖口，至曩已移日。

translations.literal: The Jingchu method actually errs regarding the five planets; now they are at syzygy, yet days ago the sun had already shifted.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingchu calendar truly misplaces the five planets: at opposition today, the sun had already moved days earlier.

sentences.zh: 蓋略治朔望，無事檢候，是以晷漏昏明，並即《元和》，二分異景，尚不知革，日度微差，宜其謬矣。

translations.literal: It only roughly handles new and full moons without verification — hence gnomon and clepsydra, dusk and dawn all follow the Yuanhe calendar; even when the two equinoxes show different shadow lengths, they still do not know to reform; with the sun's lodge position slightly off, no wonder it is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: It only roughly fixes syzygies without observational checks, so gnomon, clepsydra, and twilight all copy the Yuanhe calendar; even when equinox shadows differ, no one reforms the system — with the sun's lodge position slightly off, error is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「《書》雲'日短星昴，以正仲冬'。

translations.literal: Dai Fazxing objected: "The Book says, 'The days are short and the star Mao culminates — thereby fixing mid-winter.'
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing objected: "The Book of Documents says, 'The days are short and the star Mao culminates — thereby fixing mid-winter.'

sentences.zh: 直以月推四仲，則中宿常在衛陽，羲、和所以正時，取其萬代不易也。

translations.literal: Simply using the months to derive the four mid-seasons, the culminating lodge is always in Wei and Yang — this is why Xi and He fixed the seasons, taking what would never change for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Derive the four mid-season months from the lunar cycle and the culminating lodge is always in Wei and Yang — this is why Xi and He fixed the seasons with a standard meant to endure forever.

sentences.zh: 沖之以為唐代冬至，日在今宿之左五十許度，遂虛加度分，空撤天路。

translations.literal: Chongzhi holds that at the Tang-era winter solstice the sun was some fifty-odd du to the left of today's lodge, and so falsely added degrees and emptied the celestial path."
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi claims the Tang-era winter solstice lay some fifty-odd du left of today's position, then invented extra degrees and emptied the celestial track."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：《書》以上四星昏中審分至者，據人君南面而言也。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi replied: When the Book uses the four stars' dusk culmination to verify the divisions and extremes, it assumes the ruler faces south.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi replied: When the Book uses four stars at dusk culmination to verify the solstices and equinoxes, it assumes the ruler faces south.

sentences.zh: 且南北之正，其詳易准，流見之勢，中天為極。

translations.literal: And the north-south alignment is easily gauged in detail; in the pattern of stars rising and setting, culmination at the meridian is the standard.
translations.idiomatic: North-south alignment is easy to judge in detail; in the cycle of rising and setting, meridian transit is the standard.

sentences.zh: 先儒注述，其義僉同，而法興以為《書》說四星，皆在衛陽之位，自在巳地，進失向方，退非始見，迂回經文，以就所執，違訓詭情，此則甚矣。

translations.literal: Earlier scholars' commentaries all agree on this point, yet Fazxing holds that the Book's four stars are all in the position of Wei and Yang, as if of themselves in the si quadrant — advancing he misses the cardinal direction, retreating he is not at first appearance; he twists the scriptural text to fit his view — this perverts the teaching and distorts the facts, and is very serious.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier commentators all agree, yet Fazxing reads the Book's four stars as fixed in Wei and Yang, as if by themselves in the si quarter — he misses the cardinal direction going forward and misstates first appearance going back; twisting scripture to fit his view perverts the text and is grave indeed.

sentences.zh: 舍午稱巳，午上非無星也。

translations.literal: Setting aside wu to call it si — above wu there are stars too.
translations.idiomatic: Set aside wu and call it si — yet stars stand above wu as well.

sentences.zh: 必據中宿，餘宿豈複不足以正時。

translations.literal: If one must rely on the culminating lodge, how could the other lodges not also suffice to fix the time?
translations.idiomatic: If only the culminating lodge counts, why could the other lodges not also fix the season?

sentences.zh: 若謂舉中語兼七列者，觜參尚隱，則不得言，昴星雖見，當雲伏矣，奎婁已見，複不得言伏見囗囗不得以為辭，則名將何附。

translations.literal: If saying "culminating" also implies all seven lodges, then when Zi and Shen are still hidden one could not speak; though Mao is visible, one would have to say it is occulted; when Kui and Lou are already visible, one could not speak of occultation and appearance — [text damaged] cannot serve as an argument — then to what would the name attach?
translations.idiomatic: If "culminating" must cover all seven lodges, then when Beak and Triplet are still hidden you could say nothing; though Mao is visible you would have to call it occulted; when Strider and Bond are already visible you could not speak of rising and setting — with such a broken argument, what could the name even attach to?

sentences.zh: 若中宿之通非允，當實謹檢經旨，直雲星昴，不自衛陽，衛陽無自顯之義，此談何因而立。

translations.literal: If the general use of "culminating lodge" is unacceptable, one should carefully examine the scriptural intent — simply say "the star Mao," not of itself Wei and Yang; Wei and Yang have no meaning of self-manifestation — on what basis does this argument stand?
translations.idiomatic: If the general rule of "culminating lodge" will not do, examine the text carefully: say simply "the star Mao," not Wei and Yang of themselves — Wei and Yang have no self-evident meaning; on what basis does this argument stand?

sentences.zh: 苟理無所依，則可愚辭成說，曾泉、桑野，皆為明證，分至之辨，竟在何日，循複再三，竊深歎息。

translations.literal: If reason has no foundation, any foolish phrase can become doctrine — Zeng Quan and Sang Ye are clear proof; the distinction of the divisions and extremes — on what day does it ultimately fall? Going over this again and again, I can only sigh deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Without rational ground any foolish phrase becomes doctrine — Zeng Quan and Sang Ye are clear proof; as for fixing the solstices and equinoxes, on what day does it finally fall? Repeating this again and again, I can only sigh.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「其置法所在，近違半次，則四十五年九月率移一度。

translations.literal: Dai Fazxing objected: "The placement of his method's reference point nearly departs by half a lodge — every forty-five years and nine months it would shift one du on average."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing objected: "His method's reference point is nearly half a lodge off — on average one du every forty-five years and nine months."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：《元和》日度，法興所是，唯征古曆在建星，以今考之，臣法冬至亦在此宿，鬥二十二了無顯證，而虛貶臣曆乖差半次，此愚情之所駭也。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi replied: The Yuanhe sun-position is what Fazxing approves — he only cites the ancient calendar placing it at Jian; examining by today's standards, my method's winter solstice is also in this lodge; southern Dipper 22 has no clear proof, yet he groundlessly denigrates my calendar as off by half a lodge — this astonishes me.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi replied: Fazxing approves the Yuanhe sun-position and cites only the ancient calendar at Jian; by today's reckoning my winter solstice is also there — Dipper 22 has no clear proof, yet he groundlessly calls my calendar half a lodge wrong; this astonishes me.

sentences.zh: 又年數之餘有十一月，而議雲九月，涉數每乖，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Further, the remainder of the year-count has an eleventh month, yet the objection says the ninth month — whenever numbers are involved they fail to match; all are of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Further, the year-count remainder includes an eleventh month, yet the objection says the ninth — whenever numbers appear they disagree; all his points are like this.

sentences.zh: 月盈則食，必在日沖，以檢日則宿度可辨，請據效以課疏密。

translations.literal: When the moon is full it eclipses, and this must be at solar opposition; checking the sun's position the lodge and degree can be determined — I ask that we rely on observed results to test coarse and fine.
translations.idiomatic: A full moon eclipses only at solar opposition; check the sun and the lodge-degree is fixed — let observed results test which method is coarse or fine.

sentences.zh: 按太史注記，元嘉十三年十二月十六日中夜月蝕盡，在鬼四度，以沖計之，日當在牛六。

translations.literal: According to the Grand Clerk's annotation: on the sixteenth day of the twelfth month of Yuanjia 13, at midnight the moon was totally eclipsed at Ghost 4th degree; by opposition calculation the sun should be at Ox 6.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Clerk records show that on Yuanjia 13, month 12, day 16, at midnight the moon was totally eclipsed at Ghost 4°; by opposition my sun should be at Ox 6.

sentences.zh: 依法興議：「在女七」。

translations.literal: By Fazxing's objection: "at Woman 7."
translations.idiomatic: By Fazxing's reckoning: "at Woman 7."

sentences.zh: 又十四年五月十五日丁夜月蝕盡，在鬥二十六度，以沖計之，日當在井三十，依法興議曰：「日在柳二。

translations.literal: Again, on the fifteenth day of the fifth month of year 14, at the ding hour the moon was totally eclipsed at Dipper 26th degree; by opposition the sun should be at Well 30; by Fazxing's objection: "the sun at Willow 2."
translations.idiomatic: Again, Yuanjia 14, month 5, day 15, at the ding hour the moon was totally eclipsed at Dipper 26°; by opposition my sun should be at Well 30; Fazxing says: "the sun at Willow 2."

sentences.zh: 」又二十八年八月十五日丁夜月蝕，在奎十一度，以沖計之，日當在角二；

translations.literal: Again, on the fifteenth day of the eighth month of year 28, at the ding hour the moon was eclipsed at Strider 11th degree; by opposition the sun should be at Horn 2;
translations.idiomatic: Again, Yuanjia 28, month 8, day 15, at the ding hour the moon was eclipsed at Strider 11°; by opposition my sun should be at Horn 2;

sentences.zh: 依法興議曰：「日在角十二。

translations.literal: By Fazxing's objection: "the sun at Horn 12."
translations.idiomatic: Fazxing says: "the sun at Horn 12."

sentences.zh: 」又大明三年九月十五日乙夜月蝕盡，在胃宿之末，以沖計之，日當在氐十二；

translations.literal: Again, on the fifteenth day of the ninth month of Daming 3, at the yi hour the moon was totally eclipsed at the end of Stomach lodge; by opposition the sun should be at Base 12;
translations.idiomatic: Again, Daming 3, month 9, day 15, at the yi hour the moon was totally eclipsed at the end of Stomach; by opposition my sun should be at Base 12;

sentences.zh: 依法興議曰：「日在心二。

translations.literal: By Fazxing's objection: "the sun at Heart 2."
translations.idiomatic: Fazxing says: "the sun at Heart 2."

sentences.zh: 」凡此四蝕，皆與臣法符同，纖毫不爽，而法興所據，頓差十度，違沖移宿，顯然易睹。

translations.literal: All four of these eclipses match my method exactly, not a hair's breadth off — yet what Fazxing relies on differs by ten full du at a stroke, violating opposition and shifting lodges — plainly visible.
translations.idiomatic: All four eclipses match my method exactly, yet Fazxing's positions differ by ten full du at once, violating opposition and shifting lodges — the mismatch is obvious.

sentences.zh: 故知天數漸差，則當式遵以為典，事驗昭晰，豈得信古而疑今。

translations.literal: Thus we know celestial numbers gradually shift — one should then take current practice as the standard; the evidence is bright and clear — how can one trust the ancient and doubt the present?
translations.idiomatic: Celestial numbers drift over time, so present practice should be the standard; the evidence is clear — how can one trust antiquity and doubt the present?

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「在《詩》'七月流火'，此夏正建申之時也。

translations.literal: Dai Fazxing objected: "In the Odes, 'In the seventh month the Fire Star flows westward' — this is when the Xia calendar takes shen as its first month.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing objected: "The Odes say, 'In the seventh month the Fire Star flows westward' — this is when the Xia calendar sets shen as its first month.

sentences.zh: '定之方中'，又小雪之節也。

translations.literal: 'Ding culminates at the center' is also the Lesser Snow node.
translations.idiomatic: 'Ding at the center' is also the Lesser Snow solar term.

sentences.zh: 若冬至審差，則豳公火流，晷長一尺五寸，楚宮之作，晝漏五十三刻，此詭之甚也。

translations.literal: If the winter solstice is truly off, then at Lord Bin's Fire Star's westward flow the gnomon shadow would be one chi five cun long, and at the building of the Chu palace the day clepsydra would mark fifty-three ke — this is extremely absurd."
translations.idiomatic: If the winter solstice were truly wrong, then when the Fire Star flows west for Lord Bin the gnomon would read one chi five cun, and when the Chu palace was built the day clepsydra would mark fifty-three ke — this is absurd in the extreme."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：臣按此議三條皆謬。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi replied: I find all three points in this objection mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi replied: I find all three points in this objection mistaken.

sentences.zh: 《詩》稱流火，蓋略舉西移之中，以為驚寒之候。

translations.literal: The Odes speak of the Fire Star flowing west — it merely cites the middle of its westward shift as a sign of coming cold.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes' "flowing Fire Star" merely marks the middle of its westward drift as a sign of coming cold.

sentences.zh: 流之為言，非始動之辭也。

translations.literal: "Flow" is not language of first motion.
translations.idiomatic: "Flow" does not mean first motion.

sentences.zh: 就如始說，冬至日度在鬥二十二，則火星之中，當在大暑之前，豈鄰建申之限。

translations.literal: Even as initially stated, if the winter solstice sun-position is at Dipper 22, then Mars's culmination would fall before Great Heat — how could it border the shen first-month limit?
translations.idiomatic: Even on his own premise — winter solstice at Dipper 22 — Mars would culminate before Great Heat, not near the shen first-month boundary.

sentences.zh: 此專自攻糾，非謂矯失。

translations.literal: This is simply self-contradictory attack — not a claim that I have falsified anything.
translations.idiomatic: This is self-contradictory attack, not proof that my method falsifies anything.

sentences.zh: 《夏小正》：「五月昏，大火中。

translations.literal: The Xia Small Calendar: "In the fifth month at dusk, the Great Fire is at culmination."
translations.idiomatic: The Xia Small Calendar says: "In the fifth month at dusk, the Great Fire culminates."

sentences.zh: 」此複在衛陽之地乎？

translations.literal: Is this again in the Wei-Yang region?
translations.idiomatic: Is that again in Wei and Yang?

sentences.zh: 又謂臣所立法，楚宮之作，在九月初。

translations.literal: He also says that by my calendar the building of the Chu palace falls at the start of the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: He also claims my calendar places the building of the Chu palace at the start of the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 按《詩》傳箋皆謂定之方中者，室辟昏中，形四方也。

translations.literal: According to the Odes commentary and annotation, "Ding at the center" means Encampment at dusk culmination forming a square.
translations.idiomatic: Odes commentary and Zheng Xuan's notes both say "Ding at the center" means Encampment culminating at dusk and forming a square.

sentences.zh: 然則中天之正，當在室之八度。

translations.literal: Thus the true meridian culmination should be at Encampment 8th degree.
translations.idiomatic: Thus true meridian culmination should fall at Encampment 8°.

sentences.zh: 臣曆推之，元年立冬後四日，此度昏中，乃處十月之初，又非寒露之日也。

translations.literal: By my calendar's calculation, four days after Start of Winter in year 1, this degree culminates at dusk — which falls at the start of the tenth month, not on Cold Dew day either.
translations.idiomatic: By my calendar, four days after Start of Winter in year 1 this degree culminates at dusk — at the start of the tenth month, not on Cold Dew.

sentences.zh: 議者之意，蓋誤以周世為堯時，度差五十，故致此謬。

translations.literal: The objector's intent seems to mistake the Zhou era for Yao's time — a fifty-du difference — hence this error.
translations.idiomatic: The objector seems to treat the Zhou era as Yao's time — a fifty-du difference — hence this error.

sentences.zh: 小雪之節，自信之談，非有明文可據也。

translations.literal: Calling it the Lesser Snow node is his own assertion — there is no explicit text to support it.
translations.idiomatic: Calling it Lesser Snow is his own assertion — no explicit text supports it.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「仲尼曰：'丘聞之，火伏而後蟄者畢。

translations.literal: Dai Fazxing objected: "Confucius said: 'I have heard that after the Fire Star is occulted, the hibernating creatures finish.'
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing objected: "Confucius said: 'I have heard that after the Fire Star is occulted, the hibernating creatures are all done.'

sentences.zh: 今火猶西流，司曆過也。

translations.literal: Now the Fire Star still flows westward — the calendar officers are at fault.'
translations.idiomatic: Now the Fire Star still flows west — the calendar officers are at fault.'

sentences.zh: '就如沖之所誤，則星無定次，卦有差方，名號之正，古今必殊，典誥之音，時不通軌。

translations.literal: If Chongzhi is as wrong as claimed, then stars would have no fixed sequence, the trigram directions would be off, the correct names would necessarily differ ancient and modern, and the sounds of the canonical pronouncements would not match the times.
translations.idiomatic: If Chongzhi is as wrong as claimed, stars would have no fixed sequence, trigram directions would shift, correct names would differ ancient and modern, and canonical sounds would no longer fit the age.

sentences.zh: 堯之開、閉，今成建、除，今之壽星，乃周之鶉尾也。

translations.literal: Yao's Kai and Bi would become today's Jian and Chu; today's Longevity Star would be Zhou's Chimei."
translations.idiomatic: Yao's Kai and Bi would become today's Jian and Chu; today's Longevity Star would be Zhou's Chimei."

sentences.zh: 即時東壁，已非玄武，軫星頓屬蒼龍，誣天背經，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Even now Eastern Wall is no longer Black Tortoise, and Corner Star suddenly belongs to Azure Dragon — to slander Heaven and violate the classics to this extent!"
translations.idiomatic: Even now Eastern Wall is no longer Black Tortoise and Corner suddenly belongs to Azure Dragon — to slander Heaven and violate the classics to this extent!"

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：臣以為辰極居中，而列曜貞觀，群像殊體，而陰陽區別，故羽介咸陳，則水火有位，蒼素齊設，則東西可准，非以日之所在，定其名號也。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi replied: I hold that the pole star sits at the center while the arrayed luminaries hold their fixed stations; the myriad figures have distinct forms while yin and yang are distinguished — hence when feathered and shelled creatures are all displayed, water and fire have their places; when azure and white are equally set out, east and west can be gauged — names are not fixed by where the sun happens to be.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi replied: The pole sits at center while the stars keep fixed stations; myriad forms differ and yin and yang are distinct — feathered and shelled creatures arrayed give water and fire their places; azure and white equally set let east and west be gauged — names are not fixed by the sun's current position.

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How is this shown?
translations.idiomatic: How is this shown?

sentences.zh: 夫陽爻初九，氣始正北，玄武七列，虛當子位。

translations.literal: The first nine of the yang line — qi starts due north; the seven stars of Black Tortoise — Emptiness holds the zi position.
translations.idiomatic: The first nine of the yang line: qi begins due north; the seven stars of Black Tortoise — Emptiness holds the zi position.

sentences.zh: 若圓儀辨方，以日為主，冬至所舍，當在玄枵；

translations.literal: If one uses the circular instrument to distinguish directions with the sun as master, where winter solstice lodges should be at Dark Emptiness;
translations.idiomatic: If the circular instrument fixes directions by the sun, winter solstice should lodge at Dark Emptiness;

sentences.zh: 而今之南極，乃處東維，違體失中，其義何附。

translations.literal: yet today's south pole sits in the eastern quadrant — violating form and losing center; what meaning can this attach to?
translations.idiomatic: yet today's south pole sits in the eastern quadrant — violating form and losing center; what meaning can attach to that?

sentences.zh: 若南北以冬夏稟稱，則卯酉以生殺定號，豈得春躔義方，秋麗仁域，名舛理乖，若此之反哉！

translations.literal: If north-south are named from the endowment of winter and summer, then mao and you should be named from life and death — how could spring dwell in the domain of Righteousness and autumn beautify the domain of Benevolence? Names contradict reason in such reversal!
translations.idiomatic: If north-south are named from winter and summer's endowment, mao and you should be named from life and death — how could spring dwell in Righteousness and autumn beautify Benevolence? Names and reason collide in such reversal!

sentences.zh: 因茲以言，因知天以列宿分方，而不在於四時，景緯環序，日不獨守故轍矣。

translations.literal: From this one knows Heaven divides directions by the lodge sequence, not by the four seasons; the sun rides the circuit of nodes and girdle-stars — it does not alone keep to its old track.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know Heaven divides directions by lodge sequence, not by the four seasons; the sun rides the circuit of nodes and girdle-stars — it does not keep to its old track alone.

sentences.zh: 至於中星見伏，記籍每以審時者，蓋以歷數難詳，而天驗易顯，各據一代所合，以為簡易之政也。

translations.literal: As for culminating stars' appearance and occultation, records often use them to verify seasons — because calendar numbers are hard to detail while celestial tests are easy to show; each age relies on what fits its time as a simple practical policy.
translations.idiomatic: Records often use culminating stars' risings and settings to verify seasons because calendar arithmetic is hard to detail while sky tests are easy to show — each age uses what fits its time as a practical shortcut.

sentences.zh: 亦猶夏禮未通商典，《濩》容豈襲《韶》節，誠天人之道同差，則藝之興，因代而推移矣。

translations.literal: Just as Xia ritual did not yet merge with Shang canon, how could the Huo dance follow the Shao rhythm? Truly if Heaven and human ways share the same drift, then the arts arise and shift with each era.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Xia ritual had not yet merged with Shang canon, how could the Huo dance follow the Shao rhythm? If Heaven and human ways drift together, the arts shift with each era.

sentences.zh: 月位稱建，諒以氣之所本，名隨實著，非謂鬥杓所指。

translations.literal: Calling the moon's position "jian" surely follows the qi it is rooted in — the name follows what is real, not what the Dipper handle points to.
translations.idiomatic: Calling the moon's position "jian" follows the qi it is rooted in — the name tracks reality, not the Dipper handle's aim.

sentences.zh: 近校漢時，已差半次，審鬥節時，其效安在。

translations.literal: Comparing with Han times recently, it already differs by half a lodge — verify the Dipper-node seasons: where is the effect?
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Han times it already differs by half a lodge — test Dipper-node seasons: where is the proof?

sentences.zh: 或義非經訓，依以成說，將緯候多詭，偽辭間設乎？

translations.literal: Or if the meaning is not from classical teaching but relied on to make doctrine — are apocryphal prognostications mostly deceitful, with false phrases inserted here and there?
translations.idiomatic: Or if meaning not drawn from the classics is used to make doctrine — are apocryphal prognostications mostly deceit, with false phrases inserted here and there?

sentences.zh: 次隨方名，義合宿體。

translations.literal: Lodge sequence follows directional names — the meaning fits the lodge bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Lodge sequence follows directional names — the meaning fits the lodge bodies themselves.

sentences.zh: 分至雖遷，而厥位不改，豈謂龍火貿處，金水亂列，名號乖殊之譏，抑未詳究。

translations.literal: Though divisions and extremes migrate, their positions do not change — how could one say Azure Dragon and Fire trade places, or Metal and Water fall into disorder? The reproach of mismatched names has not been examined in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Though solstices and equinoxes migrate, their positions do not change — how could Azure Dragon and Fire trade places, or Metal and Water fall into disorder? The charge of mismatched names has not been examined.

sentences.zh: 至如壁非玄武，軫屬蒼龍，瞻度察晷，實效鹹然。

translations.literal: As for Wall not being Black Tortoise and Corner belonging to Azure Dragon — observing degrees and inspecting shadows, the actual results are plainly so.
translations.idiomatic: Wall is not Black Tortoise and Corner belongs to Azure Dragon — observe degrees and inspect shadows, and the results plainly show it.

sentences.zh: 《元嘉曆法》，壽星之初，亦在翼限，參校晉注，顯驗甚眾。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia calendar method, the start of the Longevity Star was also in the Wing range — comparing with Jin-era annotations, there are many clear proofs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia calendar the Longevity Star's start was also in the Wing range — compare Jin-era notes and the proofs are many.

sentences.zh: 天數差移，百有餘載，議者誠能馳辭騁辯，令南極非冬至，望不在沖，則此談乃可守耳。

translations.literal: Celestial numbers drift over a hundred-odd years — if the objector could truly unleash rhetoric and debate to make the south pole not be winter solstice and full moon not be at opposition, then this talk could be upheld.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial numbers drift over a hundred-odd years — if the objector could truly debate away winter solstice at the south pole and full moon at opposition, then this talk might stand.

sentences.zh: 若使日遷次留，則無事屢嫌，乃臣曆之良證，非難者所宜列也。

translations.literal: If the sun's migration by lodge is allowed, there is no need for repeated objections — this is good proof of my calendar, not something the critic should raise.
translations.idiomatic: Allow the sun's lodge migration and there is no need for repeated objections — this supports my calendar; it is not a point the critic should raise.

sentences.zh: 尋臣所執，必據經史，遠考唐典，近征漢籍，讖記碎言，不敢依述，竊謂循經之論也。

translations.literal: Examining what I hold to, I always rely on classics and histories — examining Tang canon in the distance, citing Han records in the near; apocryphal fragments I dare not follow — I hold this to be argument according with the classics.
translations.idiomatic: What I hold always rests on classics and histories — Tang canon in the distance, Han records near at hand; apocryphal fragments I dare not follow — this is argument according with the classics.

sentences.zh: 月蝕檢日度，事驗昭著，史注詳論，文存禁閣，斯又稽天之說也。

translations.literal: Testing sun-position by lunar eclipse — the evidence is bright and clear; historical annotations discuss it in detail, the text stored in the forbidden archives — this too is reasoning grounded in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Testing sun-position by lunar eclipse — the evidence is clear; historical notes discuss it in detail and the text rests in the forbidden archives — this too is reasoning grounded in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《堯典》四星，並在衛陽，今之日度，遠淮元和，誣背之誚，實此之謂。
