translations.literal: The four stars of the Canon of Yao are all placed in Wei and Yang; today's sun-position departs far from the Yuanhe standard — the reproach of slander and violation refers precisely to this.
translations.idiomatic: The four stars of the Canon of Yao are all placed in Wei and Yang; today's sun-position departs far from the Yuanhe standard — the charge of slander and violation refers precisely to this.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「夫日有緩急，故鬥有闊狹，古人制章，立為中格，年積十九，常有七閏，晷或盈虛，此不可革。

translations.literal: Dai Fazxing objected: "The sun has slow and fast phases, hence the Dipper span has wide and narrow — the ancients made the intercalation rule and set the mean standard: over nineteen accumulated years there are always seven intercalations; gnomon shadows may be surplus or deficit — this cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Fazxing objected: "The sun has slow and fast phases, so the Dipper span has wide and narrow parts — the ancients made the intercalation rule and set the mean standard: over nineteen years there are always seven leap months; gnomon shadows may run surplus or deficit — this cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 沖之削閏壞章，倍減餘數，則一百三十九年二月，於四分之科，頓少一日；

translations.literal: Chongzhi trims intercalations and ruins the rule, halving the remainders — then in the 139th year, second month, under the Quarter-Remainder system, suddenly one day short;
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi trims intercalations and ruins the rule, halving the remainders — then in year 139, month 2, under the Quarter-Remainder system, suddenly one day short;

sentences.zh: 七千四百二十九年，輒失一閏。

translations.literal: in 7,429 years one intercalation would be lost.
translations.idiomatic: in 7,429 years one intercalation would be lost.

sentences.zh: 夫日少則先時，閏失則事悖。

translations.literal: If days are fewer, events come early; if intercalations are lost, affairs are contradicted.
translations.idiomatic: Fewer days mean events come early; lost intercalations mean affairs fall out of step.

sentences.zh: 竊聞時以作事，事以厚生，此乃生民之所本，歷數之所先。

translations.literal: I have heard that seasons serve to do work, and work serves to nourish life — this is the root of the people and the first of calendar numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Seasons serve work, and work nourishes life — this is the people's foundation and the first concern of calendar reckoning.

sentences.zh: 愚恐非沖之淺慮，妄可穿鑿。

translations.literal: I fear this is not Chongzhi's shallow thought that one may rashly carve and bore."
translations.idiomatic: I fear this is not shallow thinking that one may rashly carve and bore."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：按《後漢書》及《乾象說》，《四分曆法》，雖分章設篰創自元和，而晷儀眾數定于嘉平三年。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi replied: According to the History of the Later Han and the Qianxiang Treatise, the Quarter-Remainder calendar method — though its intercalation rule and bamboo tallies were first devised in the Yuanhe era — its gnomon instrument and various constants were fixed in the third year of Jiaping.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi replied: The History of the Later Han and Qianxiang Treatise show that though the Quarter-Remainder intercalation rule and bamboo tallies began in the Yuanhe era, its gnomon constants were fixed in Jiaping 3.

sentences.zh: 《四分志》，立冬中影長一丈，立春中影九尺六寸。

translations.literal: The Quarter-Remainder treatise: at mid-term of Start of Winter the shadow is one zhang; at mid-term of Start of Spring, nine chi six cun.
translations.idiomatic: The Quarter-Remainder treatise: at Start of Winter mid-term the shadow is one zhang; at Start of Spring mid-term, nine chi six cun.

sentences.zh: 尋冬至南極，日晷最長，二氣去至，日數既同，則中影應等，而前長後短，頓差四寸，此曆景冬至後天之驗也。

translations.literal: Seeking winter solstice at the south pole, the gnomon is longest; the two qi are equidistant from the solstice and the day-counts are the same — thus mid-term shadows should be equal, yet the former is long and the latter short, suddenly differing four cun — this is proof the calendar's solstice shadow puts winter solstice late.
translations.idiomatic: At winter solstice the gnomon is longest; Start of Winter and Start of Spring are equidistant from solstice with equal day-counts — mid-term shadows should match, yet the first is longer and the second shorter by four cun — proof the calendar places winter solstice late.

sentences.zh: 二氣中影，日差九分半弱，進退均調，略無盈縮。

translations.literal: Mid-term shadows of the two qi differ by nine fen and a little under — advance and retreat are evenly adjusted, scarcely any surplus or deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-term shadows of the two qi differ by nine fen and a fraction — advance and retreat are evenly adjusted, with scarcely any surplus or deficit.

sentences.zh: 以率計之，二氣各退二日十二刻，則晷影之數，立冬更短，立春更長，並差二寸，二氣中影俱長九尺八寸矣。

translations.literal: Calculating by rate, if each qi retreats two days twelve ke, then the gnomon numbers — Start of Winter shorter, Start of Spring longer — would both differ two cun, and mid-term shadows of both qi would be nine chi eight cun.
translations.idiomatic: By rate, if each qi retreats two days twelve ke, Start of Winter shadows shorten and Start of Spring lengthen by two cun each — both mid-term shadows become nine chi eight cun.

sentences.zh: 即立冬、立春之正日也。

translations.literal: That is the true day of Start of Winter and Start of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Those are the true days of Start of Winter and Start of Spring.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，曆置冬至，後天亦二日十二刻也。

translations.literal: From this one infers the calendar's placement of winter solstice puts it two days twelve ke late.
translations.idiomatic: From this the calendar's winter solstice is two days twelve ke late.

sentences.zh: 嘉平三年，時曆丁醜冬至，加時正在日中。

translations.literal: In Jiaping 3, the calendar of the time had winter solstice on dingchou, the added hour exactly at midday.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaping 3 the calendar placed winter solstice on dingchou with the added hour exactly at midday.

sentences.zh: 以二日十二刻減之，天定以乙亥冬至，加時在夜半後三十八刻。

translations.literal: Subtracting two days twelve ke, Heaven fixes winter solstice on yihai, the added hour thirty-eight ke after midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract two days twelve ke and Heaven fixes winter solstice on yihai, thirty-eight ke after midnight.

sentences.zh: 又臣測景曆紀，躬辨分寸，銅表堅剛，暴潤不動，光晷明潔，纖毫盡然。

translations.literal: Further, my shadow-measurement calendar record — I personally distinguished fen and cun; the bronze gnomon rigid and firm, swollen by damp it did not shift; light and shadow clear and clean, every hair's breadth evident.
translations.idiomatic: My shadow-measurement records show I personally distinguished fen and cun; the bronze gnomon was rigid and did not shift when damp; light and shadow were clear to the finest line.

sentences.zh: 據大明五年十月十日，影一丈七寸七分半，十一月二十五日，一丈八寸一分太，二十六日，一丈七寸五分強，折取其中，則中天冬至，應在十一月三日。

translations.literal: According to Daming 5: on the tenth day of the tenth month the shadow was one zhang seven cun seven fen and a half; on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month, one zhang eight cun one fen tai; on the twenty-sixth, one zhang seven cun five fen strong — taking the mean, meridian winter solstice should fall on the third day of the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Daming 5: month 10, day 10, shadow one zhang seven cun seven fen and a half; month 11, day 25, one zhang eight cun one fen tai; day 26, one zhang seven cun five fen strong — taking the mean, meridian winter solstice should fall on month 11, day 3.

sentences.zh: 求其蚤晚，令後二日影相減，則一日差率也。

translations.literal: To find whether early or late, subtract the shadows of the following two days — that gives the daily difference rate.
translations.idiomatic: To find whether solstice is early or late, subtract the shadows of the following two days — that yields the daily difference rate.

sentences.zh: 倍之為法，前二日減，以百刻乘之為實，以法除實，得冬至加時在夜半後三十一刻，在《元嘉曆》後一日，天數之正也。

translations.literal: Double it for the divisor; subtract the prior two days; multiply by one hundred ke for the dividend; divide dividend by divisor — winter solstice's added hour is thirty-one ke after midnight, one day after the Yuanjia calendar — the true celestial number.
translations.idiomatic: Double that for the divisor, subtract the prior two days, multiply by one hundred ke for the dividend, and divide — winter solstice falls thirty-one ke after midnight, one day after the Yuanjia calendar: the true celestial number.

sentences.zh: 量檢竟年，則數減均同，異歲相課，則遠近應率。

translations.literal: Measuring and checking through the full year, the reductions and counts agree uniformly; testing across different years, near and far match the rate.
translations.idiomatic: Checking through the full year, reductions and counts agree uniformly; testing other years, near and far match the rate.

sentences.zh: 臣因此驗，考正章法。

translations.literal: From this evidence I examined and corrected the intercalation rule.
translations.idiomatic: From this evidence I examined and corrected the intercalation rule.

sentences.zh: 今以臣曆推之，刻如前，竊謂至密，永為定式。

translations.literal: Now computing by my calendar, the ke as before — I hold it extremely precise, to be the fixed standard forever.
translations.idiomatic: Computing by my calendar yields the same ke as before — I hold it extremely precise and fit to be the fixed standard.

sentences.zh: 尋古曆法並同《四分》，《四分》之數久則後天，經三百年，朔差一日。

translations.literal: Examining ancient calendar methods, all matched the Quarter-Remainder; its numbers over time put Heaven late — after three hundred years, new moon differs by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient calendar methods all matched the Quarter-Remainder; over time its numbers put Heaven late — after three hundred years new moon slips one day.

sentences.zh: 是以漢載四百，食率在晦。

translations.literal: Hence over four hundred years of Han, eclipses mostly fell on the last day of the month.
translations.idiomatic: Hence over four hundred Han years, eclipses mostly fell on the last day of the month.

sentences.zh: 魏代已來，遂革斯法，世莫之非者，誠有效於天也。

translations.literal: Since the Wei era this method was reformed — the world did not fault it; it truly matched Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei this method was reformed and the world did not fault it — it truly matched Heaven.

sentences.zh: 章歲十九，其疏尤甚，同出前術，非見經典。

translations.literal: Nineteen-year intercalation rule is especially coarse — it comes from the same prior methods, not seen in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The nineteen-year intercalation rule is especially coarse — it comes from the same prior methods, not from the classics.

sentences.zh: 而議雲此法自古，數不可移。

translations.literal: Yet the objection says this method is ancient and the numbers cannot shift.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the objection says this method is ancient and the numbers cannot shift.

sentences.zh: 若古法雖疏，永當循用，謬論誠立，則法興複欲施《四分》於當今矣，理容然乎？

translations.literal: If ancient methods though coarse must forever be followed and this fallacy truly stands — then Fazxing would again want to apply the Quarter-Remainder to the present day — does reason allow this?
translations.idiomatic: If coarse ancient methods must forever be followed and this fallacy stands, Fazxing would again apply the Quarter-Remainder today — does reason allow that?

sentences.zh: 臣所未譬也。

translations.literal: This I do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: This I do not understand.

sentences.zh: 若謂今所革創違舛失衷者，未聞顯據有以矯奪臣法也。

translations.literal: If one says today's innovations violate and miss the mean, I have not heard clear evidence to overturn my method.
translations.idiomatic: If today's reforms violate the mean, I have heard no clear evidence to overturn my method.

sentences.zh: 《元嘉曆》術，減閏餘二，直以襲舊分粗，故進退未合。

translations.literal: The Yuanjia calendar method reduced the intercalary remainder by two — simply inheriting the old coarse fractions — hence advance and retreat did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanjia calendar reduced the intercalary remainder by two — simply inheriting old coarse fractions — so advance and retreat did not agree.

sentences.zh: 至於棄盈求正，非為乖理。

translations.literal: As for abandoning surplus to seek correctness — this is not contrary to reason.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoning surplus to seek correctness is not contrary to reason.

sentences.zh: 就如議意，率不可易，則分無增損，承天置法，複為違謬。

translations.literal: If one follows the objection's intent and on average nothing can be changed, then the divisions gain and lose nothing — yet setting the method according to Heaven would again be wrong and in error.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the objection to its conclusion — nothing may change on average, the solstice-equinox divisions neither gain nor lose — and yet a calendar ordained by Heaven becomes wrong again. The contradiction is plain.

sentences.zh: 節氣蚤晚，當循《景初》，二至差三日，曾不覺其非，橫謂臣曆為失，知日少之先時，未悟增月甚惑也。

translations.literal: As for solar terms early or late, one should follow the Jingchu calendar; the two solstices differ by three days, yet they never notice their error and arbitrarily claim my calendar is wrong — they perceive that fewer days make the time early, but do not grasp that adding months is deeply confusing.
translations.idiomatic: Solar terms early or late should follow the Jingchu calendar, you say — yet the two solstices are three days off and you never notice; you denounce my calendar while grasping that fewer days bring events early, but not that piling on months breeds worse confusion.

sentences.zh: 誠未睹天驗，豈測歷數之要，生民之本，諒非率意所斷矣。

translations.literal: Having truly not seen celestial verification, how can one measure the essentials of calendar reckoning — the foundation of the people? Surely this is not something to be decided at will.
translations.idiomatic: Without ever looking to the sky for proof, how can one judge the heart of calendar reckoning — the foundation of the people? That surely is not a matter for arbitrary decree.

sentences.zh: 又法興始雲窮識晷變，可以刊舊革今，複謂晷數盈虛，不可為准，互自違伐，罔識所依。

translations.literal: Further, Fazxing first said he fully understood gnomon changes and could revise the old and reform the present, then again said gnomon numbers surplus and deficit cannot serve as standard — contradicting himself, with no idea what to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Fazxing first claimed he had mastered gnomon change and could cut the old and shape the new — then declared gnomon surplus and deficit unfit for a standard. He contradicts himself and knows not what to stand on.

sentences.zh: 若推步不得准，天功絕於心目，未詳曆紀何 因而立。

translations.literal: If calculation cannot match, the work of Heaven is cut off from eye and mind — I do not see on what basis the calendar era could be established.
translations.idiomatic: If computation cannot hit the mark, Heaven's work is blind to eye and mind alike — on what basis, then, was the calendar era ever erected?

sentences.zh: 案《春秋》以來千有餘載，以食檢朔，曾無差失，此則日行有恆之明征也。

translations.literal: Examining from the Spring and Autumn Annals for more than a thousand years, checking new moons by the eclipse records, there has never been error — this is clear proof that the sun's daily motion is constant.
translations.idiomatic: From the Spring and Autumn Annals down through a thousand years and more, new moons checked against eclipse records have never missed — bright proof that the sun's daily motion is constant.

sentences.zh: 且臣考影彌年，窮察毫微，課驗以前，合若符契，孟子以為千歲之日至，可坐而知，斯言實矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, I have measured shadows for a full year, examining the finest details; tested against earlier records, they match like seal and tally. Mencius held that the solstice of a thousand years hence can be known while seated — this saying is true.
translations.idiomatic: I have measured shadows through a full year, scrutinizing the finest lines; checked against prior records, they fit like seal and tally. Mencius said the solstice a thousand years hence can be known while seated — and he spoke true.

sentences.zh: 日有緩急，未見其證，浮辭虛貶，竊非所懼。

translations.literal: The sun's slow and fast phases — I have not seen proof of them; empty words and baseless denigration — I confess I do not fear.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's slow and fast phases — I have seen no proof. Empty rhetoric and hollow slander — those I do not fear.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「沖之既雲冬至歲差，又謂虛為北中，舍形責影，未足為迷。

translations.literal: Fazxing argued: "Chongzhi already says the winter solstice shifts year by year, yet also holds Emptiness as north-center — abandoning form and relying on shadow, this is not enough to count as error."
translations.idiomatic: Fazxing argued: "Chongzhi claims the winter solstice drifts year by year, yet also makes Emptiness the northern center — abandoning form for shadow alone. That hardly proves him wrong."

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 凡在天非日不明，居地以鬥而辨，借令冬至在虛，則黃道彌遠，東北當為黃鐘之宮，室壁應屬玄枵之位，虛宿豈得複為北中乎？

translations.literal: Whatever is in heaven is unclear without the sun; on earth one distinguishes by the Dipper — suppose winter solstice were at Emptiness, then the Yellow Track would be farther still; the northeast should be the palace of Yellow Bell, Roof and Wall should belong to Dark Establishment — how could Emptiness lodge again be north-center?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's signs are dark without the sun; on earth we orient by the Dipper. Grant winter solstice at Emptiness — the Yellow Track recedes farther still; the northeast should be Yellow Bell's palace, Roof and Wall Dark Establishment's seat — how could Emptiness lodge be north-center again?

sentences.zh: 曲使分至屢遷，而星次不改，招搖易繩，而律呂仍往，則七政不以璣衡致齊，建時亦非攝提所紀，不知五行何居，六屬安托。

translations.literal: Forcing the solstices and equinoxes to shift repeatedly while star sequence does not change, moving the polar-indicator's cord while pitch-pipes stay the same — then the seven luminaries would not be aligned by the armillary sphere, the founding of seasons would not be marked by Raghorn either; one would not know where the Five Phases dwell or where the six domains attach.
translations.idiomatic: Force the solstices and equinoxes to wander while star sequence stands still, swing the polar cord while pitch-pipes hold their course — then the seven luminaries no longer align by the armillary sphere, seasons no longer open under Raghorn's mark; the Five Phases lose their seats, the six domains their moorings.

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：此條所嫌，前牒已詳。

translations.literal: " Chongzhi said: "The grievance in this point has already been treated in detail in my earlier memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi replied: "This objection was already answered at length in my earlier memorial."

sentences.zh: 次改方移，虛非中位，繁辭廣證，自構紛惑，皆議者所謬誤，非臣法之違設也。

translations.literal: Shift of sequence and change of direction — Emptiness is not the center; verbose arguments and broad proofs only construct confusion — all are the objector's mistakes, not flaws in my method's design.
translations.idiomatic: Sequence shifts and directions move — Emptiness is no center. Verbose proofs only weave confusion. These are the objector's errors, not faults in my method's design.

sentences.zh: 七政致齊，實謂天儀，鄭、王唱述，厥訓明允，雖有異說，蓋非實義。

translations.literal: "Seven luminaries aligned" refers to the celestial instrument; Zheng Xuan and Wang Su expounded it — their teaching is clear and apt; though there are differing views, they are surely not the real meaning.
translations.idiomatic: "Seven luminaries aligned" means the celestial instrument itself. Zheng Xuan and Wang Su taught it clearly; other readings exist, but they are not the real meaning.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「夫置元設紀，各有所尚，或據文於圖讖，或取效於當時。

translations.literal: Fazxing argued: "In establishing origin and setting era, each has its preference — some rely on apocryphal texts, some take effect from the present age."
translations.idiomatic: Fazxing argued: "Every calendar sets its origin and era by its own lights — some from apocryphal charts, some from what works in the present age."

sentences.zh: 沖之雲'群氏糾紛，莫審其會。

translations.literal: Chongzhi says "the many schools dispute, none discerning the conjunction."
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi says, "Schools dispute and none can fix the conjunction."

sentences.zh: '昔《黃帝》辛卯，日月不過，《顓頊》乙卯，四時不忒，《景初》壬辰，晦無差光，《元嘉》庚辰，朔無錯景，豈非承天者乎？

translations.literal: "In the past the Yellow Emperor calendar had xinmao — sun and moon did not err; Zhuanxu had yimao — four seasons were not off; Jingchu had renchen — last days had no wrong brilliance; Yuanjia had gengchen — new moons had no mistaken shadows — are these not calendars that matched Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: "The Yellow Emperor calendar at xinmao — sun and moon never strayed; Zhuanxu at yimao — seasons never missed; Jingchu at renchen — month-ends without false light; Yuanjia at gengchen — new moons without wrong shadow. Were these not calendars that truly matched Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 沖之苟存甲子，可謂為合以求天也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi, if he merely preserves jiazi, can be said to have forced a match to seek Heaven's approval."
translations.idiomatic: If Chongzhi merely clings to jiazi, he has forced a fit to win Heaven's favor."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：夫曆存效密，不容殊尚，合讖乖說，訓義非所取，雖驗當時，不能通遠，又臣所未安也。

translations.literal: " Chongzhi said: Calendar reckoning requires close effect and precision — it cannot tolerate separate preferences; matching apocrypha and contradicting teaching — the exegetical meaning is not what I take; though verified in its time, it cannot extend to the distant future — this too is what I am not at ease with."
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi replied: A calendar must be precise in its effects — it cannot serve separate tastes. Matching apocrypha while betraying exegesis I will not take; what fits one age may fail the distant future — and that too I cannot accept.

sentences.zh: 元值始名，體明理正。

translations.literal: The origin's value is in its founding name — the principle is clear and right.
translations.idiomatic: An origin earns its name at the founding — the principle is lucid and sound.

sentences.zh: 未詳辛卯之說何依，古術詭謬，事在前牒，溺名喪實，殆非索隱之謂也。

translations.literal: I do not know what the xinmao claim rests on; the ancient methods are absurd — this was treated in my earlier memorial; drowning in names and losing substance — hardly what seeking hidden meaning means.
translations.idiomatic: I do not see what the xinmao claim rests on. Those ancient methods are absurd — I treated them in my earlier memorial. Drowning in names while losing substance is hardly "seeking the hidden."

sentences.zh: 若以曆合一時，理無久用，元在所會，非有定歲者，今以效明之。

translations.literal: If a calendar matches only one moment, by reason it cannot long serve; the origin lies where conjunctions fall — there is no fixed year-count — now let effectiveness clarify this.
translations.idiomatic: If a calendar fits only one moment, reason says it cannot endure. The origin sits where conjunctions fall — there is no fixed year-count. Let present proof decide.

sentences.zh: 夏、殷以前，載籍淪逸，《春秋》漢史，鹹書日蝕，正朔詳審，顯然可徵。

translations.literal: Before Xia and Yin, records were lost; the Spring and Autumn Annals and Han histories all record solar eclipses — the first day of the month is detailed and can be clearly verified.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xia and Yin, records were lost. The Spring and Autumn Annals and Han histories record solar eclipses in detail — new moons plainly verifiable.

sentences.zh: 以臣曆檢之，數皆協同，誠無虛設，循密而至，千載無殊，則雖遠知矣。

translations.literal: Checking by my calendar, the numbers all agree — truly no empty setup; proceeding with precision through the ages, for a thousand years without difference — then even the distant is knowable.
translations.idiomatic: Checked against my calendar, the numbers all agree — no empty artifice. Proceed with precision and a thousand years show no drift — even the far past becomes knowable.

sentences.zh: 備閱曩法，疏越實多，或朔差三日，氣移七晨，未聞可以下通於今者也。

translations.literal: Having reviewed past methods, their looseness is indeed great — some differ three days on new moon, solar terms shift seven mornings — I have not heard that any can extend down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Past methods, reviewed in full, are loose in the extreme — new moons off by three days, solar terms by seven mornings. None, I hear, can stretch down to our day.

sentences.zh: 元在乙丑，前說以為非正，今值甲子，議者複疑其苟合，無名之歲，自昔無之，則推先者，將何從乎？

translations.literal: When the origin was in yichou, earlier critics called it incorrect; now at jiazi, objectors again suspect forced matching — a year without canonical name has never existed before — then those who push antiquity, from what will they proceed?
translations.idiomatic: When the origin stood at yichou, critics called it wrong; now at jiazi they cry forced fit again. A nameless year never existed in antiquity — then on what will antiquarians stand?

sentences.zh: 曆紀之作，幾於息矣。

translations.literal: The making of calendar eras would nearly cease.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar-making would nearly come to a halt.

sentences.zh: 夫為合必有不合，願聞顯據，以核理實。

translations.literal: To force a match there must always be a mismatch — I wish to hear clear evidence to verify truth and fact.
translations.idiomatic: Every forced fit hides a misfit. I ask for clear evidence to test truth against fact.

sentences.zh: 法興曰：「夫交會之元，則蝕既可求，遲疾之際，非凡夫所測。

translations.literal: Fazxing said: "The origin of conjunctions — then eclipses can be sought; the juncture of slow and fast — this is not what ordinary men can measure."
translations.idiomatic: Fazxing said: "Fix the origin of conjunction and eclipses follow; the juncture of slow and fast lies beyond ordinary reckoning."

sentences.zh: 昔賈逵略見其差，劉洪粗著其術，至於疏密之數，莫究其極。

translations.literal: In the past Jia Kui glimpsed the difference, Liu Hong roughly set forth the method — as for the numbers coarse and fine, none have reached the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui once glimpsed the difference; Liu Hong roughly sketched the method. As for coarse and fine numbers, none have reached the limit.

sentences.zh: 且五緯所居，有時盈縮，即如歲星在軫，見超七辰，術家既追算以會今，則往之與來，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the five girdle-stars' positions at times swell and shrink — just as when Jupiter is at Axle, its appearance leaps seven lodges; since computists already trace calculation to match the present, past and future can surely be known.
translations.idiomatic: The five girdle-stars swell and shrink in their stations — Jupiter at Axle, visible, leaps seven lodges. Since astronomers trace calculation to the present, past and future are surely known.

sentences.zh: 《景初》所以紀首置差，《元嘉》兼又各設後元者，其並省功於實用，不虛推以為煩也。

translations.literal: Why Jingchu placed the difference at the era start and Yuanjia additionally set later origins — both save effort for practical use, not empty extrapolation for needless trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu placed its difference at the era head; Yuanjia added later origins — both to save labor for practical use, not to spin empty extrapolation.

sentences.zh: 沖之既違天于改易，又設法以遂情，愚謂此治曆之大過也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi both violated Heaven in reform and designed methods to suit his wishes — I deem this the great fault in governing calendar reckoning."
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi both defied Heaven in reform and shaped methods to his whim — the gravest fault in calendar governance."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：遲疾之率，非出神怪，有形可檢，有數可推，劉、賈能述，則可累功以求密矣。

translations.literal: " Chongzhi said: The ratios of slow and fast do not come from spirits and marvels — they have form that can be inspected, numbers that can be derived; since Liu and Jia could set them forth, one can accumulate effort to seek precision."
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi replied: Slow-fast ratios are not born of spirits — they have form to inspect and numbers to derive. Liu and Jia laid the groundwork; one may pile effort until precision is won.

sentences.zh: 議又雲「五緯所居，有時盈縮」。

translations.literal: The objection again says "the five girdle-stars' positions at times swell and shrink."
translations.idiomatic: The objection repeats: "The five girdle-stars swell and shrink in their stations."

sentences.zh: 「歲星在軫，見超七辰」。

translations.literal: "When Jupiter is at Axle, its appearance leaps seven lodges."
translations.idiomatic: "When Jupiter is at Axle, visible, it leaps seven lodges."

sentences.zh: 謂應年移一辰也。

translations.literal: This means it should shift one lodge per year.
translations.idiomatic: He means it should move one lodge each year.

sentences.zh: 案歲星之運，年恆過次，行天七匝，輒超一位。

translations.literal: Examining Jupiter's course: each year it always overshoots its station; circling heaven seven times, it then leaps one position.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter's course: each year it overshoots its station; seven circuits of heaven, then one leap forward.

sentences.zh: 代以求之，曆凡十法，併合一時，此數咸同，史注所記，天驗又符。

translations.literal: Seeking by successive ages, among some ten calendar methods all converging on one moment — this number is everywhere the same; historical notes record it, and celestial verification again matches.
translations.idiomatic: Track it age by age — ten calendar methods, all converging on one moment. The number is everywhere the same; histories record it, the sky confirms it.

sentences.zh: 此則盈次之行，自其定準，非為衍度濫徙，頓過其沖也。

translations.literal: This is the course of surplus in station — it has its fixed standard; it is not reckless extrapolation and random shifting, suddenly overshooting in one bound.
translations.idiomatic: This is surplus motion by fixed rule — not reckless extrapolation, not a sudden leap past opposition in one bound.

sentences.zh: 若審由盈縮，豈得常疾無遲。

translations.literal: If it truly arose from swell and shrink, how could it always be fast and never slow?
translations.idiomatic: If swell and shrink truly ruled it, how could it run always fast and never slow?

sentences.zh: 夫甄耀測象者，必料分析度，考往驗來，准以實見，據以經史。

translations.literal: Those who select luminaries and measure the sky must estimate and analyze degrees, examine past and verify future, take actual observation as standard, and ground in classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Those who read the stars must analyze degrees, test past against future, take what the eye sees as standard, and anchor in classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 曲辯碎說，類多浮詭，甘、石之書，互為矛盾。

translations.literal: Tortured arguments and fragmentary talk are mostly hollow and devious; the books of Gan and Shi contradict each other.
translations.idiomatic: Tortured arguments and broken phrases are mostly hollow trickery; Gan and Shi's books contradict each other.

sentences.zh: 今以一句之經，誣一字之謬，堅執偏論，以罔正理，此愚情之所未厭也。

translations.literal: Now with one line of scripture to slander one character's error, stubbornly holding a partial view to obscure right reason — this is what my plain mind has never been able to accept.
translations.idiomatic: One line of scripture to convict one character's flaw, a partial view held stubbornly to blind right reason — my plain mind has never stomach for this.

sentences.zh: 算自近始，眾法可同，但《景初》之二差，承天之後元，實以奇偶不協，故數無盡同，為遺前設後，以從省易。

translations.literal: Calculation begins from the near — all methods can agree; only Jingchu's two differences, inheriting the later origin after Chengtian, truly because odd and even did not accord, hence numbers could not be wholly identical — they left the earlier and set the later for ease and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation starts from the near — all methods may agree. Only Jingchu's twin differences, inheriting Chengtian's later origin, failed because odd and even would not align; numbers could not match wholly, so they kept the earlier and set the later for simplicity.

sentences.zh: 夫建言倡論，豈尚矯異，蓋令實以文顯，言勢可極也。

translations.literal: In offering proposals and raising debate, why would one prize perverse difference? It is simply to let fact show through words — the rhetorical force can be taken to its limit.
translations.idiomatic: In debate one does not prize perversity for its own sake — one lets fact shine through words until the argument reaches its limit.

sentences.zh: 稽元曩歲，群數鹹始，斯誠術體，理不可容譏；

translations.literal: Tracing the origin to past years, all numbers begin together — this is truly the body of the art; by reason it cannot be faulted;
translations.idiomatic: Trace the origin to antiquity and all numbers begin together — this is the body of the art; reason itself forbids faulting it;

sentences.zh: 而譏者以為過，謬之大者。

translations.literal: yet those who fault it call it a fault — the greatest error.
translations.idiomatic: yet critics call it fault — the greatest error of all.

sentences.zh: 然則《元嘉》置元，雖七率舛陳，而猶紀協甲子，氣朔俱終，此又過謬之小者也。

translations.literal: Then Yuanjia's setting of origin — though its seven ratios were wrongly set out, still its era matched jiazi and qi and new moon all terminated together — this was the lesser fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia's origin-setting — seven ratios wrongly arrayed, yet era, qi, and new moon all closed on jiazi — that was the lesser fault.

sentences.zh: 必當虛立上元，假稱曆始，歲違名初，日避辰首，閏餘朔分，月緯七率，並不得有盡，乃為允衷之制乎？

translations.literal: Must one empty establish a superior origin, falsely call it calendar beginning, let years violate the founding name, sun avoid the era head, intercalary remainder and new-moon fraction, moon-path and seven ratios — all have no end — before it counts as a balanced system?
translations.idiomatic: Must one hollowly erect a superior origin, falsely name the calendar's birth, let years betray the founding name, the sun flee the era head, intercalary remainder and new-moon fraction, moon-path and seven ratios all without end — before the system is judged balanced?

sentences.zh: 設法情實，謂意之所安；

translations.literal: Designing methods for truth and fact — that is what the mind can rest in;
translations.idiomatic: Methods shaped to truth and fact — that is what the mind can rest in;

sentences.zh: 改易違天，未睹理之譏者也。

translations.literal: "Reform violates Heaven" — I have not seen the reason in that reproach.
translations.idiomatic: "Reform defies Heaven" — I see no reason in that reproach.

sentences.zh: 法興曰：「日有八行，合成一道，月有一道，離為九行，左交右疾，倍半相違，其一終之理，日數宜同。

translations.literal: Fazxing said: "The sun has eight paths that merge into one track; the moon has one path split into nine paths — left is conjunction, right is fast, half and double mutually diverge; in the principle of one cycle completing, the day-counts should be the same."
translations.idiomatic: Fazxing said: "The sun runs eight paths that merge into one track; the moon one path split into nine — left conjunction, right fast, half and double at odds. When one cycle completes, the day-counts should match."

sentences.zh: 沖之通同與會周相覺九千四十，其陰陽七十九周有奇，遲疾不及一匝，此則當縮反盈，應損更益。

translations.literal: Chongzhi's unified conjunction cycle feels nine thousand forty short compared to the synodic period; its yin-yang seventy-nine cycles plus a fraction — the slow-fast does not reach one full circuit — then what should shrink swells, what should decrease increases."
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi's unified conjunction cycle falls nine thousand forty short of the synodic period; yin-yang runs seventy-nine cycles and a fraction while slow-fast never completes one circuit — what should shrink swells, what should decrease grows."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：此議雖遊漫無據，然言跡可檢。

translations.literal: " Chongzhi said: This objection, though wandering and unsupported, yet its words and traces can be inspected."
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi replied: This objection wanders without ground — yet its words leave traces that can be inspected.

sentences.zh: 按以日八行譬月九道，此為月行之軌，當循一轍，環匝於天，理無差動也。

translations.literal: Taking the sun's eight paths as analogy to the moon's nine paths — this is the track of the moon's motion; it should follow one rut, circling heaven — by reason there is no deviation.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's eight paths mirror the moon's nine — the moon's track. It should follow one rut, wheeling through heaven without deviation.

sentences.zh: 然則交會之際，當有定所，豈容或鬥或牛，同麗一度。

translations.literal: Then at the moment of conjunction there should be a fixed place — how could it sometimes be Dipper, sometimes Ox, both occupying one degree?
translations.idiomatic: At conjunction there must be a fixed place — how could it be Dipper one time, Ox another, both sharing one degree?

sentences.zh: 去極應等，安得南北無常。

translations.literal: Distance from the pole should be equal — how could north and south be without fixed rule?
translations.idiomatic: Distance from the pole should be equal — how could north and south lack fixed rule?

sentences.zh: 若日月非例，則八行之說是衍文邪？

translations.literal: If sun and moon are not the pattern, then is the doctrine of eight paths mere interpolated text?
translations.idiomatic: If sun and moon are not the pattern, is the eight-path doctrine mere interpolated text?

sentences.zh: 左交右疾，語甚未分，為交與疾對？

translations.literal: "Left conjunction, right fast" — the language is quite unclear: does it mean conjunction opposes fast?
translations.idiomatic: "Left conjunction, right fast" — the phrase is unclear. Does conjunction oppose fast?

sentences.zh: 為舍交即疾？

translations.literal: Or that setting aside conjunction is just fast?
translations.idiomatic: Or does setting conjunction aside mean fast alone?

sentences.zh: 若舍交即疾，即交在平率入曆七日及二十一日是也。

translations.literal: If setting aside conjunction is just fast, then conjunction at mean rate entering the ephemeris on the seventh and twenty-first days is the case.
translations.idiomatic: If setting conjunction aside is fast alone, then conjunction at mean rate enters the ephemeris on the seventh and twenty-first days.

sentences.zh: 值交蝕既當在盈縮之極，豈得損益，或多或少。

translations.literal: When conjunction coincides with eclipse it should be at the extreme of swell and shrink — how could there be increase or decrease, more or less?
translations.idiomatic: When conjunction meets eclipse it should sit at swell-shrink extremes — how could increase or decrease vary, more or less?

sentences.zh: 若交與疾對，則在交之沖，當為遲疾之始，豈得入曆或深或淺，倍半相違，新故所同，複摽此句，欲以何明。

translations.literal: If conjunction opposes fast, then at conjunction's opposite it should be the start of slow and fast — how could entering the ephemeris be sometimes deep, sometimes shallow, half and double mutually divergent? Ancient and modern share this — again citing this line, to clarify what?
translations.idiomatic: If conjunction opposes fast, opposition should mark slow-fast beginnings — how could ephemeris entry run deep or shallow, half and double at odds? Old and new calendars agree here — why cite this line, and to prove what?

sentences.zh: 臣覽曆書，古今略備，至如此說，所未前聞，遠乖舊准，近背天數，求之愚情，竊所深惑。

translations.literal: I have reviewed calendar books ancient and modern, largely complete — to such a saying I have never heard before; far from old standards, near violating celestial numbers — seeking this in my plain mind, I confess deep perplexity.
translations.idiomatic: I have read calendar books ancient and modern, nearly complete — never heard such a claim. It deserts old standards and defies present numbers; searched with my plain mind, I confess deep bewilderment.

sentences.zh: 尋遲疾陰陽不相生，故交會加時，進退無常，昔術著之久矣，前儒言之詳矣。

translations.literal: Slow-fast and yin-yang do not generate each other — hence at conjunction the added hour, advance and retreat are without fixed rule; former methods recorded this long ago, earlier scholars spoke of it in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Slow-fast and yin-yang do not beget each other — so conjunction hours advance and retreat without fixed rule. Old methods recorded this; earlier scholars spoke at length.

sentences.zh: 而法興雲日數同。

translations.literal: Yet Fazxing says the day-counts are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fazxing says the day-counts match.

sentences.zh: 竊謂議者未曉此意，乖謬自著，無假驟辯，既雲盈縮失衷，複不備記其數，或自嫌所執，故泛略其說乎？

translations.literal: I privately think the objector has not understood this meaning — the error shows by itself, with no need for hurried debate; having said swell and shrink miss the mean, yet again not fully recording the numbers — or does he distrust his own position, and so vaguely abbreviate his argument?
translations.idiomatic: I think the objector has not grasped this — the error shows itself, no hasty rebuttal needed. He claims swell-shrink misses the mean yet will not set the numbers down — or does he doubt his own case and vaguely trim his words?

sentences.zh: 又以全為率，當互因其分，法興所列二數皆誤，或以八十為七十九，當縮反盈，應損更益，此條之謂矣。

translations.literal: Again, taking the whole as rate, one should mutually follow its parts — both numbers Fazxing listed are wrong; perhaps taking eighty for seventy-nine — what should shrink swells, what should decrease increases — this is what that point means.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the whole as rate, one must follow its parts — both numbers Fazxing lists are wrong; perhaps eighty for seventy-nine. What should shrink swells, what should decrease grows — that is what his point amounts to.

sentences.zh: 總檢其議，豈但臣曆不密，又謂何承天法乖謬彌甚。

translations.literal: Examining his objections in sum — not only is my calendar imprecise, he also says He Chentian's method is wrong in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, his objections declare not only my calendar imprecise but He Chentian's method wrong in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 若臣曆宜棄，則承天術益不可用。

translations.literal: If my calendar should be discarded, then Chentian's art is even less usable.
translations.idiomatic: If my calendar must go, Chentian's art is even less usable.

sentences.zh: 法興所見既審，則應革創。

translations.literal: If Fazxing's judgment is so clear, then reform should follow.
translations.idiomatic: If Fazxing's judgment is so sure, let him reform the calendar.

sentences.zh: 至非景極，望非日沖，凡諸新說，必有妙辯乎？

translations.literal: As for apogee not at Jing, full moon not at solar opposition — for all such new claims, surely there must be brilliant arguments?
translations.idiomatic: Apogee not at Jing, full moon not at solar opposition — for every novel claim, surely there must be brilliant arguments?

sentences.zh: 時法興為世祖所寵，天下畏其權，既立異議，論者皆附之。

translations.literal: At that time Fazxing was favored by Emperor Xiaowu; the realm feared his power — once he raised a different view, debaters all attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fazxing then stood in Emperor Xiaowu's favor; the realm feared his power. Once he raised dissent, every debater fell in behind him.

sentences.zh: 唯中書舍人巢尚之是沖之之術，執據宜用。

translations.literal: Only Palace Secretariat Attendant Chao Shangzhi upheld Chongzhi's method, holding that evidence favored its adoption.
translations.idiomatic: Only Palace Secretariat Attendant Chao Shangzhi upheld Chongzhi's method and argued the evidence favored adoption.

sentences.zh: 上愛奇慕古，欲用沖之新法，時大明八年也。

translations.literal: The emperor loved the novel and admired antiquity, and wished to adopt Chongzhi's new method — it was the eighth year of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved the novel and revered antiquity; he wished to adopt Chongzhi's new method — in the eighth year of Daming.

sentences.zh: 故須明年改元，因此改曆。

translations.literal: Hence the next year would change the era name, and thereby reform the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The next year would change the era name and, with it, the calendar.

sentences.zh: 未及施用，而宮車晏駕也。

translations.literal: Before it could be implemented, the imperial carriage came to its evening halt — the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Before it could take effect, the imperial carriage halted at evening — the emperor was dead.
